A diagonal matrix is always what type of matrix?
A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries only on the main diagonal, and a main diagonal exists only for a square matrix. So every diagonal matrix is a square matrix.
An identity matrix is a special diagonal matrix in which every diagonal entry is 1.
Abdul Qadir was a famous player of which sport?
Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.
Abdul Qadir played 67 Tests for Pakistan and died in 2019.
Abdul Sattar Edhi is associated with which city of Pakistan?
Edhi made Karachi the base of his welfare work, and the Edhi Foundation is headquartered there.
Edhi was born in Bantva, Gujarat (India) in 1928 and died in 2016.
According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected?
By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.
The Electoral College initially had 80,000 members, later raised to 120,000 (equally from East and West Pakistan).
What type of government was set up by the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
The 1962 constitution concentrated executive power in the President, so it created a presidential form of government.
The 1973 constitution replaced it with a parliamentary system.
According to the 1973 Constitution, how many houses does the Parliament of Pakistan have?
The Parliament consists of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house), plus the President.
The Senate has 96 members after the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP.
According to the 1973 Constitution, who resolves a dispute between the National Assembly and the Senate?
Under Article 70, a bill on which the two houses disagree is settled by a joint sitting of both houses, decided by a majority of the total members present.
The President summons the joint sitting.
According to the Islamic calendar, in which month did Pakistan become independent?
Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramazan 1366 AH, a Friday and the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) according to common belief.
Ramazan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
After how many years of independence did Pakistan get its first constitution?
Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, nearly 9 years later.
23 March was celebrated as Republic Day, and the 1956 constitution was abrogated in 1958 by Ayub Khan.
The Khilafat Movement started after which event?
The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.
Its leaders included Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali.
Against whom did Shahid Afridi score his record 37-ball century in 1996?
Afridi hit the then fastest ODI century off 37 balls against Sri Lanka at Nairobi in October 1996.
The record stood for 18 years until broken by Corey Anderson in 2014 and then by AB de Villiers.
Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought?
The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.
Hazrat Ali conquered the fort of Qamus in this battle.
Against whom was the Battle of Tabuk fought?
In 9 AH the Prophet (PBUH) led an army to Tabuk to face the Byzantine force, but no fighting took place.
It was the last military expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).
Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country?
Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.
Some candidates thought it was Egyptian, but it is Qatari.
Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.
Khalid bin Waleed is known as Saifullah (Sword of Allah).
At what age (approximately) did the last revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Revelation began when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 and continued for about 23 years, so the last revelation came at about age 63.
Most scholars say the last verses were revealed a few weeks before his death at 63.
In front of whose house did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat to Madina?
The Prophet (PBUH) left the camel free and it knelt near the house of Abu Ayub Ansari, so he stayed there.
The Prophet (PBUH) stayed there until the Masjid-e-Nabawi and his rooms were built.
Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place?
The Bolan Pass is a natural route in Balochistan linking Quetta with the plains of Sibi and Dadhar.
Khojak Pass, not Bolan, links Quetta with Chaman and Afghanistan.
Boris Johnson served as Prime Minister (2019-2022) of which country?
Boris Johnson led the Conservative Party and was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from July 2019 to September 2022.
He is no longer in office, having resigned in 2022 and been followed by Liz Truss.
By whom was the Objectives Resolution passed?
It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 12 March 1949.
It later became the preamble of the 1956, 1962 and 1973 constitutions in some form.
By whose hand was Hazrat Hamza martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
Wahshi bin Harb, a slave of Jubayr bin Mutim, killed Hazrat Hamza with a spear on the order of Hind.
The Coastal Highway connects Gwadar with which city?
The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Arabian Sea coast from Karachi to Gwadar.
It is about 653 km long and was completed in 2004.
The Danube is the second longest river of which continent?
The Danube, about 2,850 km long, is the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.
It flows into the Black Sea.
Desert Fox is the title of whom?
Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name Desert Fox for his skilled command of the German Afrika Korps in North Africa.
He was defeated by Montgomery at El Alamein in 1942.
Diphtheria is a disease of which part of the body?
Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and upper airways.
It is prevented by the DPT vaccine.
Fill in the blank: He wasted his time ___ TV.
After the expression waste time, the gerund (-ing form) is used, so watching is correct.
The same pattern is used in spend time doing something.
Fill in the blank: The Pacific is ___ than the Arctic Ocean.
The sentence compares two things and uses than, so the comparative deeper is needed.
The Pacific is the deepest and largest ocean on Earth.
For the Khilafat Movement, Muslims of India migrated towards which country?
During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Muslims left India for Afghanistan as a protest against British rule.
The migration failed because the Afghan government could not support so many people.
For what purpose was the Khilafat Movement started?
Indian Muslims started it to save the Ottoman Caliph and the Ottoman Empire after World War I.
It began in 1919 and ended after Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
From which institution did Quaid-e-Azam obtain his law degree?
Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.
He was the youngest Indian to be called to the bar at that time.
From which city did the Urdu-Hindi controversy start in 1867?
In 1867 Hindus of Banaras demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in government offices, starting the controversy.
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan took it as a sign that Hindus and Muslims could not remain together.
From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar?
Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958 for about 3 million US dollars, and it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon was in office at the time.
The Gulf of Siam, now known as the Gulf of Thailand, mainly lies in which country?
The Gulf of Siam is the old name of the Gulf of Thailand, which borders Thailand mainly, as well as Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
Sources differ on which country to name, but Thailand is the answer given in most textbooks.
Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a Pakistani cricketer and the first captain of Pakistan in Test cricket.
He captained Pakistan in its first Test victory, at The Oval in 1954.
Harappa, a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization, was situated on the bank of which river?
Harappa lies in Sahiwal district of Punjab beside the (now partly dried) bed of the River Ravi.
Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus city, stood on the bank of the Indus in Sindh.
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom?
Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom?
Hazrat Hafsa (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA).
The first written compilation of the Quran was kept with her during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA) and later.
Hazrat Hajra (Hajar) was the mother of which prophet?
Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ismail (AS).
The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates her search for water.
Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of which prophet?
Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), who was born without a father by Allah's command.
Surah Maryam, the 19th surah of the Quran, is named after her.
Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which tribe?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Quraish tribe, to its clan Banu Hashim.
Banu Aws and Banu Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina who became the Ansar.
How many ayats (verses) does Surah Al-Fatiha, the first surah of the Quran, have?
Surah Al-Fatiha has seven ayats, which is why it is also called Sab'a al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated verses).
Some candidates remembered 5 but the correct number is 7.
How many ayats were revealed in the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The first revelation in the Cave of Hira consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
The first revelation came in the month of Ramadan.
How many continents are there in the world?
The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania).
Asia is the largest continent and Australia the smallest.
How many copies of the Quran were prepared in the era of Hazrat Usman (RA)?
Hazrat Usman (RA) had the Quran copied in a standard text and copies were sent to the main centres, commonly given as seven in Pakistani textbooks.
Sources differ: some give 4, 5 or 7 copies; the standard text is known as Mushaf-e-Usmani.
How many member states does the European Union (EU) have?
The EU has 27 member states, and the number has not changed since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020.
Before Brexit the EU had 28 members; Croatia was the last to join, in 2013.
How many daughters did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) have?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA).
All of his daughters except Hazrat Fatima (RA) died during his lifetime.
Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) were killed in the Battle of Badr?
About 70 Quraish fighters were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr.
Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr.
How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of ghusl are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
The three faraiz of ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.
The faraiz of wudu are four in Hanafi fiqh.
How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to and including the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet up to the ankles.
The faraiz of ghusl are three.
How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) perform after his migration to Madina?
He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage).
He delivered his Farewell Sermon on the plain of Arafat during this Hajj.
How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there?
They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
Their combined rule lasted about 30 years (632 to 661 AD).
How many Makki surahs are there in the Quran?
Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.
Sources differ slightly on the exact numbers, but 86 and 28 are the figures most Pakistani textbooks give.
How many original members did the United Nations have when it was founded in 1945?
The UN began in 1945 with 51 original member states (Poland signed later and is counted among them).
How many Muslims were in the army at the Battle of Uhad (Uhud) in the end?
About 1000 set out, but Abdullah bin Ubayy withdrew with about 300 men, leaving about 700 Muslims.
The Quraish army at Uhad numbered about 3000.
How many non-permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
The Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.
How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
The permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each holding veto power.
Russia took the Soviet Union's seat in 1991 and China's seat passed from Taiwan to the PRC in 1971.
How many pillars of Islam are there?
The five pillars are Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
Salah is the pillar performed five times daily.
How many planets are there in the solar system?
There are eight planets since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
The planets in order from the Sun start with Mercury and end with Neptune.
How many players are there in a football team on the field?
A football team fields eleven players including the goalkeeper.
A standard football match lasts 90 minutes.
How many rukus are there in the Holy Quran (Pakistani edition)?
Pakistani printed copies of the Quran are divided into 540 rukus, marked by the letter Ain in the margin.
Counts differ in other editions (for example 558 in Arabic prints).
How many seats of the National Assembly of Pakistan are reserved for women?
Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.
Another 10 seats are reserved for non-Muslims.
How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was born to Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq (AS) to Hazrat Sarah.
How many surahs does the Quran have?
The Quran has 114 surahs, from Al-Fatiha to An-Nas.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest and Surah Al-Kausar the shortest.
How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup?
Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
Pakistan is the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history.
How many ayats are there in total in Surah Al-Baqarah?
Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, has 286 ayats.
It is the second surah of the Quran.
For how many years did the Holy Prophet (SAW) live in Madina after the Hijrah?
He migrated to Madina in 622 AD (1 AH) and passed away there in 632 AD (11 AH), about ten years later.
He lived about 13 years in Makkah after receiving the first revelation.
In how many fields is the Nobel Prize awarded today?
The Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics, which is six fields.
Originally there were five; the Economics prize was added in 1969.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to India?
The 1960 treaty gave the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.
India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, but the treaty allocation itself is unchanged.
In which battle did Allah help the Muslims with angels?
The Quran (Surah Al-Imran and Al-Anfal) says Allah sent angels to help the Muslims at Badr.
Badr was fought in 2 AH with about 313 Muslims against about 1000 Quraish.
In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Madinah?
The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH on the advice of Salman Farsi. It stopped the Quraysh and their allies from attacking the city.
The Battle of Khandaq is also called the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab).
In which battle was Abu Jahl killed?
Abu Jahl, a leader of the Quraysh, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. He was struck down by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.
Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.
In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. He was killed by Wahshi, a slave of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.
Hazrat Hamza (RA) is known as Asadullah and Sayyid ush-Shuhada (Chief of the Martyrs).
In which battle was Hazrat Jafar Tayyar (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) was one of the three commanders martyred in the Battle of Mutah in 8 AH. He is called Tayyar (the flyer) because he is said to have been given wings in Paradise.
The other two commanders at Mutah were Zaid bin Haritha and Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA).
Near which city in Punjab are the ruins of the Indus Valley site of Harappa?
The ruins of Harappa lie near the town of Harappa in Sahiwal district of Punjab, Pakistan. The site was first excavated in the 1920s.
Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus Valley city, is in Larkana district of Sindh.
In which city of India is Jallianwala Bagh located?
Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden in Amritsar, Punjab, India. British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd there on 13 April 1919.
The massacre took place on Baisakhi day in 1919.
In which city is the historic Bala Hisar Fort located?
Bala Hisar Fort stands in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It overlooks the old city.
The fort was rebuilt by the Sikhs in the early 19th century.
In which city is the Quaid-e-Azam Residency located?
The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days there in 1948.
The Residency was originally built in 1892 as a British summer retreat.
Near which city is the Rohtas Fort located?
Rohtas Fort is near Dina in Jhelum district, Punjab. Sher Shah Suri built it in the 16th century.
Rohtas Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located?
The Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
Mian Mir is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple at Amritsar at the invitation of Guru Arjan.
In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located?
The Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the walled city of Lahore. It was built in 1634-35 in the Mughal era.
It is famous for its Kashi tile work.
In which city is the Arfa Karim Tower located?
The Arfa Karim Tower is in Lahore, Punjab, near Gulberg. It is named after the young computer prodigy Arfa Karim.
Arfa Karim was the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.
In which city was the All India Muslim League founded in 1906?
The All India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 at the Muslim Educational Conference, hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan.
Its first president was Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk, and Sir Aga Khan was the first permanent president.
In which country does the Orange River mainly flow?
The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa and flows westward to the Atlantic Ocean. It rises in the mountains of Lesotho.
It forms part of the border between South Africa and Namibia.
In which country is the volcano Mount Etna located?
Mount Etna is on the island of Sicily, Italy. It is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.
It is the highest active volcano in Europe.
In which country were the 2016 Olympic Games held?
The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
They were the first Summer Olympics held in South America.
In which country were the Olympic Games postponed from 2020 and held in 2021 hosted?
The Tokyo Olympics, scheduled for 2020, were postponed because of Covid-19 and held in Japan in July-August 2021.
The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris in 2024.
In which direction of Pakistan is India located?
India lies along the eastern border of Pakistan.
The Pakistan-India border is about 2,900 km long.
In which direction of Pakistan is Iran located?
Iran lies to the west of Pakistan, bordering Balochistan.
Pakistan also shares borders with Afghanistan in the west and north-west and China in the north.
In which Chinese city did the Covid-19 outbreak first appear in December 2019?
The first cases of Covid-19 were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, China, in December 2019.
The World Health Organization declared Covid-19 a pandemic in March 2020.
In which game is the agricultural shot played?
The agricultural shot is a cricket stroke in which the batsman swings the bat across the line in a cow-corner heave, like a farmer swinging a scythe.
It is usually aimed towards the cow corner region of the field.
In which Ghazwa did angels come to help the Muslims?
The Quran says that angels helped the Muslims in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1,000 Quraysh at Badr.
In which Ghazwa were the blessed teeth of the Prophet (PBUH) martyred?
The Prophet's (PBUH) front tooth was broken and he was wounded in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
The Battle of Uhud took place near Mount Uhud close to Madinah.
In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH (629 CE), before the conquest of Makkah. Some sources give 7 AH, so sources differ, but 8 AH is the common textbook answer.
He was later given the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).
In which Hijri year did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
The martyrdom of Hazrat Hussain (RA) at Karbala took place on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE).
Yazid ibn Muawiya was the Umayyad ruler at that time.
In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
It was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.
In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Battle of Uhud fought?
The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD) near Mount Uhud, a year after Badr.
The archers left their post on the hill, which let the Quraish attack from behind.
In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered?
The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
The conquest followed the Quraysh breaking the Treaty of Hudaibiya.
In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa of Khyber fought?
The Battle of Khyber was fought in 7 AH (628 CE) against the Jewish fortresses north of Madinah.
Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus at Khyber.
In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed?
The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraysh in Dhul Qadah 6 AH (628 CE).
The Quran calls it a clear victory (Fath-e-Mubin) in Surah Al-Fath.
In which language did Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai write poetry?
Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.
His famous collection of poetry is called Shah Jo Risalo.
In which month did the 1965 Pakistan-India war take place and how long did it last?
The war began on 6 September 1965 when India crossed the international border at Lahore, and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
Pakistan celebrates 6 September every year as Defence Day.
In which Islamic month is Eid ul Azha celebrated?
Eid ul Azha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
Eid ul Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.
In which Islamic month was the Quran first revealed?
The Quran began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on Laylat ul Qadr, in the cave of Hira.
The first revealed verses are the opening of Surah Al-Alaq.
In which months does the monsoon season occur in Pakistan?
The monsoon rains reach Pakistan in July and last until about September.
Most of the monsoon rain falls in the northern and north-eastern parts of the country.
In which mountain range is K2, the second highest peak in the world, located?
K2 (8,611 m) lies on the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.
K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen and Chogori.
In which province is Keenjhar Lake located?
Keenjhar Lake is near Thatta in Sindh.
Keenjhar is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan and a main water source for Karachi.
In which province is the Kharan Desert located?
The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
Pakistan's first nuclear test site, Chagai, is also in Balochistan close to this desert region.
In which province is Khanpur Dam located?
Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
In which quadrant does the point (-2, -3) lie?
Both the x-coordinate (-2) and the y-coordinate (-3) are negative, which is the third quadrant.
In the second quadrant x is negative and y is positive.
Which is the last surah of the Holy Quran?
Surah An-Nas is number 114 and is the last surah in the order of the Quran.
The first surah in order is Al-Fatihah.
In which surah is Ayat-ul-Kursi found?
Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran with 286 verses.
In which war was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 defending the BRB canal sector near Lahore.
In which year did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
The Hijrah took place in 622 AD, the 13th year of prophethood.
The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.
In which year did India carry out its first nuclear test?
India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.
India carried out further tests, Pokhran-II, in May 1998.
In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
The UN itself was founded in 1945.
In which year did Pakistan co-host the ICC Cricket World Cup together with India and Sri Lanka?
The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.
Pakistan also co-hosted the 1987 World Cup with India only.
In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
Pakistan became a member of NAM in 1979 at the Havana summit.
NAM was founded in 1961 at Belgrade.
In which year did Pakistan join SEATO?
Pakistan joined the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in 1954 when the Manila Pact was signed in September 1954.
Some sources give 1955 (ratification), and Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (CENTO) in 1955.
In which year did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.
The OIC was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011.
In which year was the OIC founded?
The OIC was founded in September 1969 at Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, at the persuasion of Allama Iqbal, Wazir Hasan and others. He remained a member of the Indian National Congress at the same time.
He left the Congress in 1920 over differences with Gandhi's policies.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die?
Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.
He is buried at Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim League reply to the Nehru Report.
They demanded safeguards for Muslims such as separate electorates and a federal system.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress?
Jinnah left Congress in 1920 over the Nagpur session and its non-cooperation policy.
He joined the Muslim League in 1913.
In which year did the Khilafat delegation led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar go to England?
The delegation went to England in 1920 to plead the case of the Ottoman Caliphate before Prime Minister Lloyd George.
The Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919.
In which year did the Quit India Movement start?
Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
The Muslim League opposed it and its slogan was Divide and Quit.
The Olympic Games were cancelled in which year of World War 1?
The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of the war; the games are held every four years, so 1914 was not an Olympic year.
The Olympics were cancelled again in 1940 and 1944 during World War 2.
In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted as the Government of India Act?
The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
The Government of India Act 1935 later introduced provincial autonomy.
In which Hijri year was the Battle of Khyber (Khaybar) fought?
The Battle of Khaybar was fought in 7 AH (628 AD) against the Jewish fortresses of Khaybar.
Hazrat Ali is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus in this battle.
In which year was NATO founded?
NATO was founded by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington in April 1949.
The Soviet-led rival Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955.
In which year was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.
