The Caspian Sea is larger but is usually not counted as a European lake.
What is the largest lake of the world by area?
The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square km, is the largest inland body of water and is classed as a lake.
Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest.
What is the largest ocean in the world?
The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square km, roughly a third of the Earth.
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest point on Earth.
What is the largest river of Afghanistan?
The Helmand River, about 1,150 km, is the longest river wholly within Afghanistan.
The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border and is not entirely within Afghanistan.
What is the longest (largest) river of Asia?
The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest river in Asia.
It is the third longest river in the world.
What is the largest river of Pakistan?
The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan.
It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.
Which is the largest sea in the world by area?
The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square km, larger than any other sea.
Candidates answered South China Sea (about 3.5 million square km), which ranks lower; some textbooks differ.
What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket?
The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.
The maximum width of the blade is 4.25 inches.
What is the length of a marathon race?
The standard marathon distance is 26 miles 385 yards, which is 42.195 km.
The distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics.
What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan?
Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.
It is shared between Sindh (about 270 km) and Balochistan (about 770 km).
What is the approximate length of the Amazon River according to common textbooks?
Most textbooks give the Amazon length as about 6,400 km.
Sources differ: some measurements give up to about 6,990 km, and the Nile is often listed as longest at about 6,650 km.
What is the length of the Canada-United States border?
The border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles), the longest international land border in the world.
Note that 5,525 is the length in miles, not kilometres.
What is the length of the Indus River according to Pakistani textbooks?
Pakistani textbooks give the length of the Indus as about 3,180 km.
Sources differ: some give about 2,880 km (Britannica) or 2,900 km.
What is the length of the Pakistan-India border (including the Line of Control and Working Boundary)?
The combined length of the international boundary, Working Boundary and Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
The Radcliffe Line of 1947 defined the border between the two countries.
What is the length of the Suez Canal?
The Suez Canal is about 193 km, which is roughly 120 miles.
It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and opened in 1869.
What is the literal meaning of the word Hadith?
In Arabic, Hadith means speech, statement, report or narration.
Technically, a Hadith is a report of the words, actions or approvals of the Prophet (SAW).
What is the literal meaning of the word Quran?
That which is recited or read
The word Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite.
Al-Furqan (the Criterion) and Al-Huda (the Guidance) are other names of the Quran.
Which is the longest river of Europe?
The Volga in Russia is about 3,530 km long and is the longest river in Europe.
The Danube is the second longest river in Europe and flows through ten countries.
Which is the longest river of Pakistan?
The Indus is about 3,000 km long and flows the whole length of Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.
The Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej are its main tributaries in the Punjab.
What is the lower house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
The National Assembly is the lower house and its members are directly elected by the people.
The upper house of Pakistan's Parliament is the Senate.
What is the meaning of Al-Feel?
Al-Feel is Arabic for the elephant and is the name of Surah 105 of the Quran.
The surah describes the army of Abraha with elephants that attacked the Kaaba in the year of the Prophet's birth.
What is the meaning of Ayat?
Ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign or a verse of the Quran.
The Quran has 114 surahs and 6,236 ayat according to the common count.
What is the meaning of Badr?
Badr in Arabic means the full moon.
The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) near a well named Badr.
A flea is a small wingless jumping insect that feeds on the blood of animals.
Fleas can jump many times their own body length.
A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
Hudaibiya is a place near Makkah where the treaty between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraish was signed in 6 AH.
The Treaty of Hudaibiya set a ten-year truce and paved the way for the conquest of Makkah.
What is the meaning of Ijtihad?
To exert effort to reach a legal ruling
Ijtihad means to strive or exert one's utmost effort, in Islamic law to derive a ruling from the Quran and Sunnah.
Allama Iqbal called ijtihad the principle of movement in Islam.
What is the meaning of Islam?
Submission to the will of Allah
Islam means submission and obedience to Allah, and the root also gives the sense of peace.
A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.
What is the meaning of Jihad?
Jihad comes from an Arabic root meaning to strive or struggle in the way of Allah.
Scholars divide it into the struggle against one's own desires and the struggle in defence of the faith.
What is the meaning of Maghfirat?
Maghfirat is Arabic for forgiveness or pardon.
Allah's name Al-Ghafoor means the Most Forgiving.
What is the meaning of the word obvious?
Something obvious is easy to see or understand and is clear to everyone.
Its opposite is obscure or hidden.
What is the meaning of Quran?
Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite, so it means that which is recited.
The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.
What is the meaning of Riba in Islam?
Riba means increase and refers to interest or usury on loans, which Islam prohibits.
The prohibition of riba is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah.
What is the meaning of Zakat?
Zakat means purification and growth, as paying it purifies a person's wealth.
Zakat is paid at 2.5 percent of savings held above the nisab for a year.
What is the most populated city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
Peshawar is the provincial capital and the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by population.
Mardan is among the next largest cities of the province.
What is the multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number A?
The multiplicative inverse of A is the number which gives 1 when multiplied by A. Since A times 1/A = 1, it is 1/A.
Which pamphlet did Chaudhry Rehmat Ali write in 1933?
Chaudhry Rehmat Ali wrote the pamphlet Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever in 1933.
In it he coined the name Pakistan.
Who was the father of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah.
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Who was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates Hajra's search for water.
What is the name of Pakistan's unmanned combat aerial vehicle?
Burraq is the armed drone developed by Pakistan and was first used in combat in 2015.
Shahpar is another Pakistani drone used mainly for surveillance.
What is the border line between Pakistan's Punjab and India's Punjab called?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 and divides Punjab between Pakistan and India.
The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
What is the name of the parliament of Finland?
The parliament of Finland is called the Eduskunta.
Storting is Norway's parliament and Riksdag is Sweden's.
What is the name of the parliament of Japan?
The national parliament of Japan is called the Diet (Kokkai).
The Diet has two houses, the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.
What is the national bird of the USA?
The bald eagle was chosen as the national bird and emblem of the United States.
It appears on the Great Seal of the United States adopted in 1782.
What is the national bird of Pakistan?
The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
The Shaheen (falcon) is the national symbol of Pakistan's air force and a popular emblem, but not the national bird.
What is the national drink (juice) of Pakistan?
Sugarcane juice is regarded as the national juice or drink of Pakistan.
Pakistan is among the world's top producers of sugarcane.
What is the national flower of Pakistan?
Jasmine (Chambeli) is the national flower of Pakistan.
Its Latin name is Jasminum officinale.
What is the national fruit of Pakistan?
The mango is the national fruit of Pakistan.
Pakistan is among the largest producers of mangoes in the world.
What is the national game of Canada?
Canada officially declared lacrosse its national summer sport and ice hockey its national winter sport in 1994.
Ice hockey is also an official national sport, so questions may accept either depending on the options.
What is the national game of Pakistan?
Field hockey is commonly given as the national game of Pakistan.
Pakistan has won the Hockey World Cup four times.
What is the national language of Pakistan?
Urdu is the national language of Pakistan under the Constitution.
English and Urdu are the official languages.
What is the national tree of Pakistan?
The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.
Its name comes from Sanskrit and means timber of the gods.
Constitutional proposals for India drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru
The Nehru Report of 1928 was a set of constitutional proposals drafted by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru. It rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
Muhammad Ali Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.
What is the number of pillars of Islam?
The five pillars are Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.
The pillars are mentioned in the well-known hadith of Ibn Umar.
In the usual order of the oceans by size, what is the number of the Indian Ocean?
By size the order is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic, so the Indian Ocean is third.
The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.
What was the old name of Attock city?
Attock city was known as Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell.
Its old name was restored to Attock in 1978.
What was the old name of Faisalabad?
Faisalabad was called Lyallpur after Sir James Lyall.
It was renamed in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
What was the old name of Madina?
Madina was known as Yathrib before the Prophet (PBUH) migrated there in 622 CE.
Madina means the city of the Prophet.
What was the old name of Sri Lanka?
Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon until it was renamed in 1972.
Burma is the old name of Myanmar and Siam of Thailand.
Which is the oldest university of Pakistan?
The University of the Punjab, Lahore was founded in 1882 and is the oldest in Pakistan.
The University of Karachi was founded in 1951.
What is the opposite of the word wild?
Wild describes animals living free in nature, and its opposite is tame.
Domesticated is another word close to tame.
What is the land between two rivers called?
A doab is the strip of land between two converging rivers.
The Punjab has five doabs such as Rachna Doab and Bari Doab.
What is the sign of the product of a positive number and a negative number?
A positive times a negative is always negative, for example 3 x (-2) = -6.
The product of two negative numbers is positive.
The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days, is located in which place?
The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. The Quaid stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.
Ziarat is famous for its juniper forests, and the Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.
What is the real name of Imam Bukhari?
Imam Bukhari's full name was Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari. He compiled the collection Sahih al-Bukhari.
Imam Bukhari was born in 810 CE in Bukhara and his Sahih is regarded as the most authentic hadith collection.
What was the relation of Hazrat Abu Talib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Abu Talib was a son of Abdul Muttalib and so a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.
Abu Talib was the father of Hazrat Ali (RA).
What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He was also close in age and a foster brother.
Hazrat Hamza was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.
What is the relation of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) with Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).
Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra and Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah.
What was the relation of Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib was a sister of Hazrat Hamza and thus a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
She was the mother of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).
What was the relation of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Abdul Muttalib was the father of Abdullah, the Prophet's father, so he was the paternal grandfather. He looked after the Prophet after the death of his mother Hazrat Amina.
Abdul Muttalib was the chief of Quraysh and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.
What is the second pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Salah is the second.
Salah was made obligatory five times a day during the Night Journey (Miraj).
What is the third pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Zakat is the third.
Zakat is generally 2.5 percent of qualifying savings held for a year.
What is the shape of a basketball court?
A basketball court is a rectangle, 28 m long and 15 m wide in international play.
A basketball team has five players on court at a time.
Which is the shortest surah of the Quran?
Surah Al-Kausar has only 3 verses and 10 words, making it the shortest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 verses.
What is the smallest bone in the human body?
The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone, about 3 mm long.
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the body.
Which is the smallest planet of the solar system?
Mercury has a diameter of about 4,880 km, the smallest of the eight planets.
Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
What is the sound made by an eagle called?
An eagle's call is described as a screech or shrill cry.
What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel?
Ababeel is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,200 km, as announced by ISPR after its first test.
Ababeel is stated to have MIRV (multiple warhead) capability and was first tested in January 2017.
Which word is a synonym of attire?
Attire means clothes or dress, so clothing is the synonym.
Another synonym of attire is apparel.
Which word is a synonym of curious?
Curious means eager to know or learn, which is the meaning of inquisitive.
Its opposite is incurious or indifferent.
Which word is a synonym of evident?
Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.
Which word is a synonym of literal?
Literal means following the exact, word-for-word meaning, so exact is the closest synonym.
Which word is a synonym of possession?
Possession means the state of having or owning something, so ownership is a synonym.
The word can also mean a thing that is owned, such as property.
Which word is a synonym of prevalent?
Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.
Its opposite is rare or uncommon.
Which word is a synonym of wild?
Wild means living or growing in nature, not controlled by humans, which is untamed. The other options are its opposites.
Its antonym is tame or domesticated.
What is the normal term of office of the Secretary General of the United Nations?
The Secretary General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council for a five-year term, which can be renewed.
The current Secretary General is Antonio Guterres of Portugal, in office since 2017, and his term ends on 31 December 2026.
What is the title of Liaqat Ali Khan?
Liaqat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was given the title Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
Which title of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) means Mercy for all the Worlds?
Rahmatul-lil-Alameen means Mercy for the Worlds and is a title of the Prophet (PBUH) taken from the Quran, Surah Al-Anbiya.
Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.
What is the total area of Punjab (Pakistan)?
The area of Punjab province is about 205,344 square kilometres.
Punjab is the second largest province by area but the largest by population; Balochistan is the largest by area.
What is the total number of rukus in the Holy Quran?
The Quran is divided into 558 rukus (sections), a division mainly used in the Indian subcontinent.
The Quran is also divided into 30 paras.
What is the total number of Ghazwat (battles in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part personally)?
Most Pakistani textbooks give 27 Ghazwat. Sources differ, as some list 26 or 29.
The expeditions he did not attend personally are called Sariyya.
How many months are there in the Islamic calendar?
The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is lunar and has 12 months, starting with Muharram.
It began with the Hijra of the Prophet (PBUH) in 622 CE.
What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
The National Assembly has 336 seats, of which Punjab has 141 general seats.
What is the total number of surahs in the Holy Quran?
Surah Al-Fatiha is the first and Surah An-Nas is the last.
The Treaty of Versailles, which ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year?
The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 at the Palace of Versailles in France.
It imposed heavy reparations on Germany and created the League of Nations.
What are the Upper House (Senate) and Lower House (National Assembly) of Pakistan jointly called?
Together with the President, the Senate and the National Assembly form the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora.
The Senate of Pakistan has 96 members.
What is the value of cos 0 degrees?
At 0 degrees the adjacent side equals the hypotenuse, so cos 0 = 1.
Approximately what percentage of the adult human body is water?
Water makes up about 60 percent of an adult's body weight.
Infants have a higher share, around 75 percent.
Which strip of land separates Pakistan from Central Asia (Tajikistan)?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan and Central Asia.
The corridor was created as a buffer between British India and Russian Empire in the 19th century.
What type of constitution was the Constitution of 1962 of Pakistan?
The 1962 constitution, introduced by Ayub Khan, gave strong powers to the President and was presidential in nature.
It was a written constitution and was abrogated in 1969.
What type of state did Afghanistan act as for a long time between the British and Russian empires?
Afghanistan stood between British India and Tsarist Russia and served as a buffer state.
The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 as its border with British India.
What was the relation of Abu Talib with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Abu Talib was the son of Abdul Muttalib and a brother of the Prophet's father Abdullah. He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.
Abu Talib was the father of Hazrat Ali (RA) and protected the Prophet during the early years in Makkah.
Fatima Jinnah trained as a dentist and qualified from the University of Calcutta in 1923. She ran her own dental clinic in Bombay.
She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation) and contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.
What was the relation of Hazrat Urwa bin Zubair with Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
Urwa was the son of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam and Hazrat Asma, who was the sister of Hazrat Ayesha. This made Urwa her nephew.
Urwa bin Zubair is one of the seven famous jurists of Madina and a major narrator of hadith from his aunt Hazrat Ayesha.
Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded?
The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.
The failed invasion took place during the presidency of John F. Kennedy and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union.
What was the caliphate number of Hazrat Umar (RA) among the Rashidun caliphs?
The order of the Rashidun caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them). Umar was therefore the second.
Hazrat Umar (RA) ruled from 634 to 644 AD and is called Al-Farooq.
Which was the first battle fought by the Muslims?
The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
About 313 Muslims faced an army of nearly 1000 Quraish at Badr and won a decisive victory.
Which city was the first capital of Pakistan?
Karachi served as the capital from 1947 when Pakistan was created. The capital was shifted to Rawalpindi in 1959 and then to Islamabad in the 1960s.
Islamabad was built as the new capital and replaced Rawalpindi, which was the interim capital.
What was the most important event of 8 AH in Islamic history?
The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 AD). The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah and cleansed the Kaaba of idols.
The Battle of Hunain and the siege of Taif followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in the same year.
Which battle of the American Civil War, fought in 1863, was the turning point of the war?
The Battle of Gettysburg was fought in July 1863 in Pennsylvania and ended in a Union victory over the Confederate army of Robert E. Lee. It is widely seen as the turning point of the war.
Abraham Lincoln delivered the famous Gettysburg Address at the battlefield in November 1863.
What was the old (previous) name of Makkah mentioned in the Holy Quran?
The Holy Quran (Surah Al-Imran, verse 96) calls the place of the first house of worship Bakkah, which is an old name of Makkah. It was also known as Umm al-Qura.
Yathrib was the old name of Madina, not Makkah.
What was the profession of Mother Teresa?
Mother Teresa was a Roman Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950 to serve the poor and the sick.
She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was declared a saint by the Catholic Church in 2016.
What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) with Hazrat Abdul Muttalib?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, and Abu Talib was a son of Abdul Muttalib. So Hazrat Ali was his grandson.
Abdul Muttalib was also the grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), which made the two cousins.
What was the relation of Hazrat Ismail (AS) with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra. He was the elder of Ibrahim's two sons.
Father and son together raised the foundations of the Kaaba in Makkah.
What was the religion of Najashi, the king of Abyssinia (Habsha) who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia was a Christian king. He protected the Muslim emigrants and refused to hand them over to the Quraish.
The Muslims made their first migration to Abyssinia in 5th year of the Prophethood.
How many Muslim soldiers fought in the Battle of Uhud?
About 1000 men set out, but 300 hypocrites under Abdullah bin Ubayy turned back on the way. This left about 700 Muslims to fight.
The Quraish army at Uhud was about 3000 strong.
When did Namaz (salah) become farz (obligatory) for Muslims?
The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, roughly five years before the Hijrat. Before this, the Muslims offered some prayers without a fixed five-time rule.
The Prophet (PBUH) received the command of five daily prayers directly from Allah during the Miraj.
In which year did Pakistan join SEATO (South East Asia Treaty Organization)?
SEATO was formed by the Manila Pact in September 1954 and Pakistan became a founding member that year.
Pakistan also joined the Baghdad Pact (later CENTO) in 1955; SEATO was dissolved in 1977.
In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy?
Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.
Pakistan has won the Champions Trophy only once; India won the 2025 edition.
In which year did Pakistan win the ICC T20 World Cup?
Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the final at Lord's in 2009 under captain Younis Khan. It is their only T20 World Cup title.
Pakistan were runners-up in 2007 and 2022; India won the 2024 and 2026 editions.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam become president of the All India Muslim League for the first time?
Jinnah was elected president of the Muslim League at the Lucknow session in December 1916. This was the session at which the Lucknow Pact was agreed.
He later served as president again in the 1920s and 1930s and led the League until Pakistan was created.
When was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935. Sir Shah Nawaz Bhutto and others had campaigned for the separation.
The Quaid-e-Azam had included the separation of Sindh in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
In which year did Swat merge fully into Pakistan?
Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.
Swat is now part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madina take place, marking the start of the Hijri calendar?
The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which is 1 AH. The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from this event.
The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar and its first month is Muharram.
In which year did the Khilafat Movement start in India?
The movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliph and the Muslim holy places after the First World War. Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.
The movement ended after Turkey abolished the caliphate in 1924.
For what purpose is Namaz-e-Istisqa offered?
Istisqa means asking for water. Muslims offer this special prayer when there is drought and ask Allah for rain.
The prayer for a solar or lunar eclipse is called Namaz-e-Kusuf or Khusuf.
In which year was Basic Democracy introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan?
President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies system through an order in October 1959. It had a five-tier structure with 80,000 Basic Democrats who elected the president.
The scheme was abolished after Ayub Khan resigned in 1969.
In which year was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) founded?
SAARC was founded at a summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The idea was proposed by Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.
SAARC has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 during the Second World War. He offered dominion status after the war, which the Congress and the Muslim League rejected.
The Cabinet Mission was a different mission that came to India in 1946.
In which year was the first census of Pakistan held?
The first census of Pakistan was held in 1951. Later censuses were held in 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998 and 2017.
The 2017 census was the first one after nearly 19 years since the 1998 census.
In which year was the first constitution of Pakistan enforced?
The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
23 March was celebrated as Republic Day until the 1962 constitution replaced it.
In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraish in 6 AH (628 AD). It gave a ten-year truce and was called a clear victory in the Quran.
The Muslims performed Umrah the following year as agreed in the treaty.
In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed?
The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916. It was an agreement in which the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
Quaid-e-Azam was the main architect of the pact and was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity.
Between which two parties was the Lucknow Pact signed?
Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Khaksar movement
The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. Both parties agreed to a joint demand for self-government.
Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Quaid-e-Azam were the main leaders involved in making the pact.
When was the All India Muslim League established?
The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted the meeting.
Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk presided and Sir Agha Khan was the first honorary president.
In which year was the OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation) established?
The OIC was founded in September 1969 at a summit in Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
Its name was changed from Organisation of the Islamic Conference to Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in 2011.
In which city was the OIC established at the first Islamic summit in 1969?
The first Islamic summit, which created the OIC, was held at Rabat in Morocco in 1969. Jeddah is the permanent headquarters of the OIC, not the place of its founding.
The Islamic Summit held in Lahore in 1974 was the second summit of the OIC.
At what age did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) place the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) in the Kaaba?
When the Quraish rebuilt the Kaaba, they disputed who would put the Black Stone in place. The Prophet, aged 35, settled the matter by placing it on a cloth carried by all the tribal chiefs.
The Quraish called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and accepted his decision.
In which year of the Hijra was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem) to the Kaaba?
The command to turn towards the Kaaba came in 2 AH, about sixteen to seventeen months after the Hijra, while the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer in Madina.
The mosque where this happened is known as Masjid Qiblatain.
When and where was the Red Cross founded?
The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 on the initiative of Henry Dunant.
Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973 and the first general elections under it were held in March 1977.
Those elections were followed by allegations of rigging and the imposition of martial law on 5 July 1977.
Where and when was the All-India Muslim League founded?
The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference, at the house of Nawab Salimullah Khan.
Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were among its early leaders, and Sir Aga Khan was its first president.
Where are the Caucasus mountains located?
Between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
Between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf
Between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea
Between the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea
The Caucasus range lies between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea and forms a boundary between Europe and Asia.
Its highest peak is Mount Elbrus in Russia.
Where did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan.
28 May is observed every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.
Which country is the place of origin of the game of squash?
Squash originated in England at Harrow School in the 19th century.
Pakistan dominated world squash through Hashim Khan, Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan.
Where does the Karakoram Highway (KKH) start in Pakistan?
In Pakistan the Karakoram Highway is commonly described as starting at Hassan Abdal and running north through Abbottabad, Gilgit and Sost to the Khunjerab Pass.
Some sources start it at Havelian, but Pakistani textbooks usually give Hassan Abdal.
In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located (on the Indus, in Mianwali district)?
Kalabagh is in Mianwali district of Punjab, on the Indus near the boundary with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The dam has never been built because of political opposition from some provinces.
Lake Saif-ul-Malook is situated in which valley?
Lake Saif-ul-Malook lies near Naran in the Kaghan Valley, Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is at about 3,200 metres above sea level.
Lake Victoria is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa.
It is the largest lake in Africa and the source of the White Nile.
In which city is the Mahabat Khan Mosque located?
The Mahabat Khan Mosque is a Mughal-era mosque in the old walled city of Peshawar, built in the 17th century.
It was built by Mahabat Khan, a governor of Peshawar under Shah Jahan.
In which province is Manchar Lake located?
Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.
It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.
Where is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir buried?
Hazrat Mian Mir, a Qadri Sufi saint, is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
He is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple in Amritsar at the invitation of the Sikh Guru.
In which country is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj?
Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia.
Pilgrims stone the Jamarat (pillars symbolising Satan) at Mina during Hajj.
In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
Nishtar Hospital is a large teaching hospital in Multan, Punjab.
It is named after Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a Pakistan Movement leader.
In which city is Qila Bala Hisar located?
Bala Hisar is the old fort of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The present fort was rebuilt by the Sikh governor Hari Singh Nalwa in the 1830s.
In which province is Ranikot (Rani Fort) located?
Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills near Sann in Jamshoro district, Sindh.
It is often called the Great Wall of Sindh because of its long walls.
In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located?
The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.
It is famous for its blue tile work and for having no minarets.
In which city is the Badshahi Mosque located?
The Badshahi Mosque stands in Lahore opposite the Lahore Fort.
It was built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673.
Where is the Bay of Biscay located?
Atlantic Ocean, off the coasts of France and Spain
The Bay of Biscay is a gulf of the north-east Atlantic Ocean, bordered by the west coast of France and the north coast of Spain.
It is known for rough seas and strong storms.
Where is the Gulf of Siam (Gulf of Thailand) located?
The Gulf of Siam, now usually called the Gulf of Thailand, is an arm of the South China Sea bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
Bangkok lies at the head of the gulf.
Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International?
Amnesty International has its international secretariat in London.
It was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.
Where is the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond kept today?
The Koh-i-Noor is set in a crown that is part of the British Crown Jewels displayed at the Tower of London.
Pakistan, India and others have claimed that it should be returned.
Where is the headquarters of NATO?
NATO has its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
NATO was founded in 1949, and its headquarters was in Paris before 1967.
Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters?
Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.
The main naval base and Fleet Command are at Karachi.
Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
The OIC secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
Its intended permanent seat is East Jerusalem once it is liberated.
In which district is the Khewra salt mine located?
The Khewra salt mine is in Jhelum district, Punjab, in the Salt Range.
It is among the largest salt mines in the world.
Where is the shrine of Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar?
Baba Farid Ganj Shakar is buried in Pakpattan, Punjab.
He was a major Chishti Sufi saint of the 12th and 13th centuries.
Where is the shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam?
The shrine of Hazrat Shah Rukn-e-Alam is in Multan.
It is famed for its Tughlaq-era architecture.
In which city is the Pakistan Steel Mills located?
Pakistan Steel Mills was built at Pipri near Karachi with Soviet help.
It began production in the early 1980s.
In which city was the OIC formed in 1969?
The OIC was formed at the Islamic summit conference held in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
Candidates often mention Saudi Arabia because the secretariat is in Jeddah.
Which agreement was signed after the 1971 war between Pakistan and India?
The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
The Tashkent Agreement was signed after the 1965 war.
Which angel brought revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Jibrael (Gabriel, AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.
Which body regulates the distribution of Indus river system water among the provinces of Pakistan?
The Indus River System Authority (IRSA) was set up in 1992 to apportion water among the provinces under the Water Apportionment Accord.
WAPDA is responsible for water and power development projects.
Who was the first child to accept Islam?
Hazrat Ali (RA), the cousin of the Prophet, accepted Islam as a boy of about 10 years old. He was raised in the Prophet's household.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man to accept Islam.
Which city of Pakistan is called the Manchester of Pakistan?
Faisalabad is the centre of Pakistan's textile industry, like Manchester in England.
Which is the biggest city of Balochistan by population?
Quetta, the provincial capital, is by far the most populous city of Balochistan.
Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.
Which province of Pakistan is known as Bab-ul-Islam (Gateway of Islam)?
Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam because Islam first entered the subcontinent there with Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 AD.
The question was asked about a city, but the standard answer is the province Sindh.
Which companion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) married two of his daughters?
Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum, both daughters of the Prophet (PBUH).
For this he is known as Dhun-Nurayn (possessor of two lights).
Which continent is called the ice desert?
Antarctica receives very little precipitation and is covered in ice, so it is called the ice desert.
It is the coldest, driest and windiest continent.
Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC?
SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Myanmar is not a member.
SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985 and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
Which country was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.
The JF-17 is jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
Ban Ki-moon, former Secretary-General of the United Nations, belongs to which country?
Ban Ki-moon is a South Korean diplomat who served as UN Secretary-General from 2007 to 2016.
He was succeeded as Secretary-General by Antonio Guterres of Portugal.
Which country awards the Nobel Prizes (apart from the Peace Prize)?
The Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature are awarded in Sweden, in line with Alfred Nobel's will.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
Which country hosted the 2016 Summer Olympic Games?
The 2016 Games were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
Rio 2016 was the first Summer Olympics held in South America.
Which country hosted the Summer Olympics held in 2021 (delayed from 2020)?
The Tokyo 2020 Games were postponed because of COVID-19 and held in Tokyo, Japan, in July and August 2021.
The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris in 2024.
Which country introduced the game of squash?
Squash was invented in England at Harrow School in the 19th century.
Pakistan dominated world squash for decades through players like Hashim Khan and Jahangir Khan.
Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
The SCO has ten full members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus. Turkey is only a dialogue partner.
Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024; Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.
Which country is known as the land of a thousand lakes?
Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes, giving it this nickname.
Canada has the largest total number of lakes in the world.
Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world?
Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer.
Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world?
China produces more tea than any other country, with India second.
Kenya and Sri Lanka are the next major producers.
Which country is the largest producer of uranium in the world?
Kazakhstan has been the world's largest uranium producer since 2009, supplying over 40 percent of world output.
Canada and Australia have large uranium reserves and held the top spots before Kazakhstan.
Which country hosted the first Football World Cup in 1930?
The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.
Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.
Which country is regarded as the birthplace of modern football (soccer)?
Modern football rules were codified in England in 1863 when the Football Association was formed.
Ancient ball games such as the Chinese cuju existed earlier, so sources differ on the earliest origin.
Which day is celebrated worldwide on 8 March?
8 March is observed as International Women's Day.
The United Nations began observing it in 1975.
Which international day is observed on 21 September?
World Peace Day (International Day of Peace)
The UN International Day of Peace is observed on 21 September each year.
World Teachers Day is on 5 October and World Food Day on 16 October.
The United Nations recognises 12 July as which day?
The UN declared 12 July Malala Day in 2013, Malala Yousafzai's birthday.
World Population Day falls on 11 July.
Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by surface area?
Lake Superior in North America has a surface area of about 82,000 square kilometres, the largest among freshwater lakes.
Lake Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake and holds the most fresh water by volume.
Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by volume?
Lake Baikal in Russia holds about 20 percent of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.
Baikal is also the deepest lake in the world.
Which is the deepest lake in the world?
Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of about 1,642 metres.
Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake.
Which is the biggest natural lake of Pakistan?
Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally cited as the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan.
Keenjhar Lake is another large freshwater lake in Sindh.
Which is the biggest province of Pakistan by area?
Balochistan covers about 347,000 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan.
Punjab is the largest province by population.
Which is the biggest river of South America?
The Amazon is South America's biggest river and the largest in the world by volume of water.
The Mississippi is a river of North America.
Which city is known as the city of mosques?
Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh, is known as the City of Mosques because of its thousands of mosques.
Dhaka is also known as the city of rickshaws.
The correct word has a double c and a double m: accommodation.
Accommodate follows the same pattern with double c and double m.
The word follows the rule i before e except after c: chief.
Chef is a different word meaning a professional cook.
Which is the most populous city of Punjab, Pakistan?
Lahore is the capital of Punjab and its largest city, with over 11 million people in the 2023 census.
Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.
Which is the largest bay in the world by area?
The Bay of Bengal, about 2.2 million square km, is generally considered the largest bay in the world.
Hudson Bay is often listed as the second largest.
Which is the largest country in the world by area?
Russia covers about 17.1 million square km, more than any other country.
Canada is the second largest country by area.
Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population?
Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population (about 127 million in the 2023 census).
Sindh is the second most populous province.
Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar?
The Islamic year has twelve months and Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and last.
Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah and Muharram is the first month.
Which is the longest freshwater lake in the world?
Lake Tanganyika in Africa is about 676 km long, the longest freshwater lake in the world.
Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world.
Which is the month of Allah (Shahrullah) in the Islamic calendar?
Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.
Some sources also apply the title Shahrullah to Muharram or Rajab, so sources differ.
Which is the most populated city of Sindh?
Karachi is the largest city of Sindh and of Pakistan by population.
Karachi is the provincial capital of Sindh.
Which is the outermost planet of the solar system?
Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Pluto was considered the ninth planet until 2006.
Which is the second largest continent by area?
Asia is the largest and Africa is second largest with about 30.3 million square km.
Africa is also the second most populous continent.
Which is the second most populous country of the world?
India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, so China is now second.
In 2021-22 China was the most populous and India second.
Australia (Oceania) has an area of about 7.7 million square km, the smallest of the continents.
Australia is the only continent that is also a single country.
Which is the world's largest uranium producing country?
Kazakhstan has been the top uranium producer since 2009 and supplied about 39 percent of world mine output in 2024.
Canada is second and Namibia third in recent World Nuclear Association data.
Which is the world's third longest river?
By length the Nile and Amazon are first and second, and the Yangtze in China is third at about 6,300 km.
The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
Which mountain range is mainly associated with Afghanistan?
The Hindu Kush range runs through central and northeastern Afghanistan into Pakistan.
Tirich Mir in Chitral is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.
Which is the highest mountain range of Pakistan?
The Karakoram range contains K2 (8,611 m), the highest peak in Pakistan.
Pakistan's mountain ranges include Himalaya, Karakoram, Hindu Kush, Sulaiman and Kirthar.
Which of the following countries is a member of SAARC?
Bhutan is one of the eight SAARC members.
SAARC members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
Which organization was formed by Turkey, Pakistan and Iran in 1964?
Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
RCD was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
Which pass connects Pakistan with China?
The Khunjerab Pass in the Karakoram links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang in China.
At about 4,693 m it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.
The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
The Khyber Pass is about 53 km long and has been an invasion and trade route for centuries.
Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly?
Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.
He is also called Dhun-Nun and Surah Younus is named after him.
Which provincial assembly of Pakistan has the most seats?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats (297 general, 66 women, 8 non-Muslim), the most of any province.
Sindh has 168, KP 145 and Balochistan 65 seats.
Which SAARC country has the highest literacy rate?
The Maldives has a literacy rate of about 98 to 99 percent, the highest among SAARC countries, with Sri Lanka close behind.
Afghanistan and Pakistan are among the lowest in SAARC for literacy.
Which Sahabi married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum?
Hazrat Usman (R.A) married Ruqayyah first and, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
He is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.
Which Sahabi served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years?
Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet as a servant at Madina as a boy and served him for about ten years.
Which sea lies between Greece and Italy?
The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
The Aegean Sea lies east of Greece, between Greece and Turkey.
Which is the biggest sea of the world by area?
The South China Sea covers about 3.5 million square km, the largest sea in the world.
The Philippine Sea is sometimes listed as larger by some sources, so sources can differ.
Which surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah?
Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
Bismillah appears twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.
Which surah is described in the Quran as Ahsan-ul-Qasas (the best of stories)?
Surah Yusuf tells the story of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S) and Allah calls it the best of stories.
Surah Yusuf is the 12th surah of the Quran.
Which Surah is known as Ash-Shifa (the cure)?
Surah Al-Fatiha is known by many names including Ash-Shifa because it is recited for healing.
It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and Sab'a al-Mathani.
In which Surah does Allah swear by time?
Surah Al-Asr begins with an oath by time (Wal-Asr).
Surah Al-Asr is the 103rd surah and has three verses.
Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
Abu Lahab is named in Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) which condemns him.
He was the only enemy of the Prophet named in the Quran.
Which was the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the first mosque of Islam in Madina?
Masjid Quba was built by the Prophet (PBUH) on his arrival near Madina during the Hijrah.
Masjid-e-Nabawi was built soon afterwards in Madina.
Which was the first prime minister of Pakistan to visit the USA?
Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950, the first Pakistani prime minister to do so.
He was Pakistan's first prime minister.
Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of a Jewish leader?
Hazrat Safiyya bint Huyayy was from the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir and married the Prophet (PBUH) after Khaybar.
She accepted Islam before the marriage.
Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A)?
Hazrat Hafsa bint Umar (R.A) married the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH.
Hazrat Aisha was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A).
Hazrat Khadija (R.A), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.
Hazrat Sumayya was the first martyr of Islam.
Which of the following is a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
The five permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China.

Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.

Who proposed digging the trench in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab)?
Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A) suggested digging a trench, a Persian defence method, to protect Madina.
The battle took place in 5 AH.
Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
The national flag was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kedwaii on the basis of the Muslim League flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947.
The green part of the flag stands for the Muslim majority and the white strip for minorities.
Who is credited with discovering the photovoltaic effect, the basis of solar energy?
Alexandre Edmond Becquerel observed the photovoltaic effect in 1839, which is the principle behind solar cells.
Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.
Who established the Mughal rule in India?
Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
Babar was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan.
Who was the first man to embrace Islam?
Among adult free men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first to accept Islam.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child to accept Islam.
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 to voice the Muslim League view.
Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
Who gave the idea of SAARC?
J. R. Jayewardene of Sri Lanka
President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh proposed regional cooperation in South Asia in 1980, leading to SAARC.
SAARC was formally founded in Dhaka in December 1985.
Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.
Who has scored the most ODI runs for Pakistan?
Inzamam-ul-Haq leads Pakistan's ODI run list with 11,701 runs.
Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him.
Which country helped Pakistan build the Chashma nuclear power plant?
The Chashma Nuclear Power Plants in Punjab were built with Chinese assistance.
China also built later units such as C-3 and C-4 at Chashma.
Which country helped the USA build relations with China in 1971?
Pakistan under Yahya Khan arranged the secret visit of Henry Kissinger to Beijing in July 1971.
President Nixon visited China in February 1972.
Who inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan?
Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.
The first governor of the State Bank was Zahid Hussain.
Who introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented it on 7 March 1949 and the Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949.
The Objectives Resolution later became the preamble and then Article 2A of the Constitution.
Who introduced the presidential system in Pakistan?
Ayub Khan introduced the presidential system through the Constitution of 1962.
Ayub Khan became Pakistan's first military ruler in 1958.
Who invented the electric bulb (practical incandescent lamp)?
Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent bulb in 1879.
Joseph Swan in Britain developed a similar lamp at about the same time.
Which company is responsible for inventing the iPhone, launched in 2007 under its co-founder Steve Jobs?
Apple Inc. launched the first iPhone in 2007, with Steve Jobs presenting it.
Steve Jobs co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in 1976.
Jibrael (AS) is the angel who brought the revelation of Allah to the prophets.
He first brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the cave of Hira.

Most Muslims of Pakistan follow the Hanafi school.
Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab?
Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024.

Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh?
Syed Murad Ali Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party has been Chief Minister of Sindh since 2016 and won a third consecutive term in 2024.
He succeeded Qaim Ali Shah, who had held the post from 2008 to 2016.
Who is the current Chairman of NAB (National Accountability Bureau)?
Lt Gen (retd) Nazir Ahmad became NAB chairman in 2023 and received a three-year extension from March 2026.
Earlier chairmen were Javed Iqbal (2017-22) and Aftab Sultan (2022-23).
Who is the Secretary General of the United Nations?
Antonio Guterres has held the post since 2017 and his term ends on 31 December 2026.

Who is the Federal Minister for Education of Pakistan?
Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui holds the Federal Education and Professional Training portfolio in 2026.
Shafqat Mahmood held the post in 2021-22 when candidates sat the test.
Who is the fastest man on earth (100 m world record holder)?
Usain Bolt of Jamaica holds the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009.

Who is the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP in Lahore in 1967.
Benazir Bhutto later became the first woman prime minister of a Muslim country.
Who is the Secretary General (head) of the Arab League?
Nabil Fahmy took office as Secretary General on 1 July 2026 for a five-year term.

Who is the national poet of Pakistan?
Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.

Who is the President of Iran?
Masoud Pezeshkian won the 2024 snap election and took office in July 2024.

Who is the President of Turkey?
Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.

Who among the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ali (RA) married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
Hazrat Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law, having married Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).
Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Army?
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Who is the writer of the novel Raja Gidh?
Raja Gidh is an Urdu novel written by Bano Qudsia.

Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?

Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942?
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call Do or Die.

Who rebuilt the Holy Kaaba with his son?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) rebuilt the Kaaba with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS).

Who signed the Tashkent Declaration on behalf of Pakistan?
President Ayub Khan signed it on 10 January 1966 with Indian PM Lal Bahadur Shastri.
Shastri died in Tashkent the next day.
Who suggested the name of the United Nations (UNO)?
US President Franklin D. Roosevelt suggested the name United Nations, first used in the Declaration of 1 January 1942.

Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth on 12 April 1961 in Vostok 1.
Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon in 1969.
Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan?
After the death of Quaid-e-Azam in September 1948, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor General of Pakistan. He held the post until 1951.

Who was the ruler of Pakistan after Yahya Khan?

Who took over as martial law administrator after Ayub Khan resigned in 1969?
Ayub Khan handed power to the army chief General Yahya Khan in March 1969, who imposed martial law.
Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948.

Who was the first captain of the Pakistan cricket team?
Abdul Hafeez Kardar captained Pakistan in its first Test series in India in 1952.

Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.

Who was the first Mughal emperor of India?
Babur founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
Sher Shah Suri was not a Mughal; he briefly defeated Humayun.
Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan in 1947 and served until 1954.

Who was the first Governor General of independent India in 1947?
Lord Mountbatten became Governor General of the Dominion of India on 15 August 1947.

Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan?
Muhammad Ali Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor General of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.

Who was the last Governor General of Pakistan?
Iskander Mirza was the last Governor General and became the first President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.
Who was the first to translate the Holy Quran into Urdu?
Shah Abdul Qadir Dehlvi produced the first idiomatic Urdu translation, Mudih-ul-Quran, in the 1790s.

Who was the first woman martyred in Islam?
Hazrat Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam.

Who was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country?
Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1988, the first woman to head a Muslim country's government.

Who was the world's first woman Prime Minister?
Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka became the world's first woman Prime Minister in 1960.
Indira Gandhi became India's Prime Minister in 1966.
Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest?

Who was the first person in space?

Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963.
Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.

Who was the first president of the All India Muslim League?
Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was the first president of the All India Muslim League, founded in Dhaka in 1906.

Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit America?
Liaquat Ali Khan visited the United States in May 1950, the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.

Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA) married the Prophet (PBUH) about 15 years before the first revelation.

Who was the first woman to accept Islam?

Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress?
Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885.

Who was the founder of the DAWN newspaper?
Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 as a voice of the Muslim League.

Who was the last Mughal emperor of India?

Who was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel?

Who was the commander of the Quraish army in the Battle of Badr?

Who won the world amateur snooker championship in 1994 for Pakistan?
Muhammad Yousaf won the IBSF World Amateur Snooker Championship in 1994.

Who was the President of the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?

Who was the second caliph (Khalifa) of Islam?

Which people lived at Khyber at the time of the Prophet (PBUH)?

Which team won the cricket World Cup in 1999?
Australia beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the 1999 final at Lord's.
Pakistan was the runner-up in 1999 and champion in 1992.
Who wrote the book Das Kapital?
Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism, was written by the German thinker Karl Marx. The first volume appeared in 1867.
Friedrich Engels edited and published the second and third volumes after Marx died.
Who wrote the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha?
Waris Shah wrote the best known version of Heer in 1766.
Earlier versions of the story were written by Damodar Gulati.
Who wrote the novel Raja Gidh?
Bano Qudsia wrote Raja Gidh, a novel about the concept of haram and halal food and its effect on the mind.

Who wrote The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam?
Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.

Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)?
Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.

Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'?

Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan?
The lyrics of Qaumi Tarana were written by the poet Abul Asar Hafeez Jalandhari. It was officially adopted in 1954.

Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal?

Gandhi refused to accept the Two-Nation Theory and the Muslim demand for Pakistan

Why do parents send their children to school?
Schools provide education, which develops knowledge, skills and character in children.
Education is a fundamental right of children under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.
Boiling heats milk enough to kill harmful germs and bacteria and makes it safe to drink and keep for longer.
Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, is the industrial process of heating milk to destroy germs.
Why is the colour of the sky blue?
Scattering of sunlight by air molecules
Absorption of blue light by clouds
Air molecules scatter short wavelength light (blue) much more than long wavelengths (red). This is called Rayleigh scattering.
At sunrise and sunset the sky looks red because light travels through more air and blue is scattered away.
With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built?
Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.
Its foundation stone was laid in 1973 and production began in 1981.
With the help of which country was Warsak Dam built?
Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was built in the 1950s with Canadian aid under the Colombo Plan.
Candidates often said China, but the dam was Canadian-assisted.
With which surah does the Holy Quran begin?
The Quran opens with Surah Al-Fatihah, which has seven verses.
Surah An-Nas is the last surah of the Quran.
Zakat is which pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj, so Zakat is third.

30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.

Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.
A median divides a triangle into two triangles of what ratio of areas?
A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so the two triangles have equal bases and the same height, hence equal areas.

Bats find their way by echolocation using high-pitched sounds.

450 degrees is one full turn plus 90 degrees.

Volume measures space in length, width and height, so it is three dimensional.

The months are January, March, May, July, August, October and December, which makes 7.

April, June, September and November have 30 days, which makes 4.

How many roots does a linear equation in one variable have?
A linear equation ax + b = 0 with a not zero has exactly one solution x = -b / a.

They are sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant and cotangent.

Each boy writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 boys write 5 pages, one page each, in 5 minutes).

The letters rearrange to BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
