She had earlier been an enemy of Islam at the Battle of Uhud.
The USSR was formed after which revolution of 1917?
The Bolshevik (October) Revolution of 1917 led by Lenin brought the communists to power, and the USSR was formally formed in 1922.
The USSR broke up in December 1991.
Against which country did Sachin Tendulkar score his 100th international century?
Tendulkar scored his 100th international century, 114 runs, against Bangladesh in the Asia Cup at Mirpur on 16 March 2012.
He is the only player to score 100 international centuries.
A number of the form a - ib, where a and b are real numbers and i is iota, is called:
Numbers written as a + ib or a - ib, with real a and b and i squared equal to -1, are complex numbers.
The numbers a + ib and a - ib are conjugates of each other.
Pakistan won the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final against which team?
Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval, London, on 18 June 2017.
Sarfraz Ahmed captained Pakistan and Fakhar Zaman scored 114 in the final.
Against whom was the Battle of Uhud fought?
The Battle of Uhud (3 AH) was fought between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah led by Abu Sufyan.
The battle took place near Mount Uhud, just north of Madinah.
Along which parallel of latitude does the border between Canada and the United States largely run (west of the Great Lakes)?
The land border from the Pacific coast to Lake of the Woods follows the 49th parallel north, set by the Treaty of 1818 and later agreements.
The 38th parallel is the better-known line that originally divided North and South Korea.
In which city was Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, born?
Arfa Karim Randhawa was born on 2 February 1995 in a village near Faisalabad, Punjab.
She died in January 2012 aged 16, and a software technology park in Lahore is named after her.
Which city hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.
The 2022 Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023 after a postponement.
In whose house in Madinah did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat?
The Prophet's camel Qaswa knelt near the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (Khalid bin Zayd), and he stayed there until his own quarters and mosque were built.
Abu Ayyub Ansari died during the Muslim siege of Constantinople and is buried near its walls.
At what age did Hazrat Ali (RA) accept Islam, according to the most commonly stated account?
Most sources say Hazrat Ali was a boy of about ten when he accepted Islam, making him among the first to do so.
Sources differ somewhat, with some giving 8 or 9 years, but 10 is the usual textbook figure.
At what age did the first revelation (wahi) come to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came at the age of 40 in the Cave of Hira.
Gabriel (Jibreel) delivered the revelation in the month of Ramadan.
At which place did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests in May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills of Balochistan on 28 and 30 May 1998.
28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.
Ateeq is the title of which companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was given the title Ateeq, meaning one freed from the Fire.
He was also called Siddiq for confirming the Prophet's journey of Miraj.
Babusar Pass connects the Kaghan Valley with which town?
Babusar Pass links Kaghan Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.
The pass is about 4,173 metres high and is usually open only in summer.
Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were tribes of which religion?
Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayzah were the Jewish tribes living around Madinah in the Prophet's time.
All three were later expelled or punished for breaking their agreements with the Muslims.
Between which two leaders was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Pakistan's President Ayub Khan and India's Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
The World Bank also signed it as a party to the treaty.
In which river is the rare blind dolphin found?
The Indus river dolphin (bhulan) is blind and lives in the Indus river system.
Its main protected stretch in Pakistan is between Guddu and Sukkur barrages.
Boxer Muhammad Ali belonged to which country?
Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer from Louisville, Kentucky.
He won the Olympic light heavyweight gold medal in Rome in 1960.
Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Under the 1973 Constitution the Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, then appointed by the President.
A candidate needs a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.
By whom are the members of the Senate of Pakistan mainly elected?
Senators from each province are elected by the members of that province's assembly through single transferable vote.
Senators serve a six-year term and half of them retire every three years.
By whom was Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal appointed governor of Yemen?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and judge around 10 AH.
The Prophet praised him as the most knowledgeable of the Ummah in halal and haram.
Masjid Zarar (Dirar) was built by which group?
A group of hypocrites built it near Quba to divide the Muslims, and the Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) condemned it.
The Prophet ordered it to be demolished after returning from Tabuk.
Campbellpur is the old name of which city of Pakistan?
The city of Attock in Punjab was called Campbellpur during British rule, after Sir Colin Campbell. It was renamed Attock in 1978.
Attock is named after the famous Attock Fort on the Indus River.
Carbon dioxide gas in the atmosphere is mainly responsible for which problem?
Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere. Increasing amounts cause the Earth to warm.
Other greenhouse gases include methane and nitrous oxide.
Chess developed from an Indian game called chaturanga around the 6th century AD. It then spread to Persia and the Muslim world.
The Arabic and Persian word shatranj comes from the Sanskrit chaturanga.
The Cholistan Desert is located near which city?
Cholistan lies in southern Punjab and stretches from Bahawalpur towards the Indian border. It is also called Rohi.
Derawar Fort is a famous landmark in the Cholistan Desert.
The COVID-19 outbreak first started in which province of China?
The first cases were reported in the city of Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, in December 2019.
The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020.
Dadu is a district of which province of Pakistan?
Dadu is a district in the northwest of Sindh, close to Lake Manchar.
The ancient site of Amri is located in Dadu district.
Deficiency of vitamin D causes which disease?
Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones. Its lack causes soft, bent bones in children, called rickets.
Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D.
Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
Vitamin A is needed to make the light-sensitive pigment in the retina. Its lack makes it hard to see in dim light.
Carrots, liver and green leafy vegetables are good sources of vitamin A.
Dr. Ruth Pfau is remembered for her work against which disease?
Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor, spent her life in Pakistan treating leprosy patients and helped control the disease.
She died in Karachi in August 2017 and was given a state funeral.
During which years did the Khilafat Movement take place in India?
The movement began in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I. It ended in 1924 when Turkey abolished the caliphate.
Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.
The ELISA test is used to diagnose which disease?
ELISA detects antibodies or antigens in blood and is the standard screening test for HIV infection. Candidates who said tuberculosis were wrong.
ELISA stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay.
Fill in the blank: ________ comes home first will cook the food.
Whoever is the subject of the clause 'comes home first' and means any person who. Whom, which and whatever do not fit.
Whoever is a compound relative pronoun.
Fill in the blank: ____ sun rises in the east.
The sun is unique, so it takes the definite article the.
The article the is also used with unique things such as the moon and the earth.
Fill in the blank: Three pictures are hanging ____ the wall.
The preposition on is used for things attached to a surface such as a wall.
We say at the door but on the wall.
Fill in the blank: He is ____ I am.
Older takes than in comparisons, and the pronoun I am follows because it is a subject comparison.
Elder is used for family members, as in elder brother, and is not followed by than.
Fill in the blank: He is accused ____ murder.
The correct phrase is accused of.
Similarly, we say suspected of and convicted of.
Fill in the blank: He is adept ____ finding flaws in the system.
Adept is followed by at (or in), meaning very skilled.
Adept is a synonym of skilled and expert.
Fill in the blank: He is deprived ____ all his money.
The correct phrase is deprived of.
Similar phrases are robbed of and bereft of.
Fill in the blank: He is jealous ____ him.
The adjective jealous takes the preposition of.
Similarly, we say envious of and afraid of.
Fill in the blank: He lived here ____ six years.
For is used with a period of time such as six years, while since is used with a point in time.
We say since 2015 but for ten years.
Fill in the blank: He reminds me ____ his teacher.
The correct phrase is remind someone of someone.
Remind someone to do something is a different pattern.
Fill in the blank: He told me that Ali ____ ill.
In reported speech after the past tense told, the present is shifts to the past tense was.
This rule of changing tense is called backshift.
Choose the correct word: I was tired, so I ____ to sleep.
The sentence is in the past tense (I was tired), so the past form went is needed.
Went is the past tense of go, and gone is its past participle.
Complete the sentence: Ali said that he ____ TV.
In reported speech after said, the present continuous is watching becomes the past continuous was watching.
Direct speech: Ali said, I am watching TV.
Complete the sentence: I am mad ____ games.
Mad about means very fond of or passionate about something.
Mad at is used when someone is angry with a person.
Fill in the blank: I ____ three books since Monday.
The word since Monday shows an action continuing up to now, so the present perfect tense is needed: have read.
The present perfect is formed with have or has plus the past participle.
Fill in the blank: I am good ____ games.
The correct preposition after good, when talking about skill, is at.
We also say bad at, clever at and quick at.
Fill in the blank with a preposition: I agreed ____ her proposal.
We agree to a proposal or plan, but agree with a person.
We agree on a matter that is being settled by several people.
Fill in the preposition: The computer is ___ the table.
An object resting on a flat surface is described with the preposition on.
In is used for enclosed spaces and at for exact points.
Fill in the preposition: The fridge is ___ the kitchen.
A room is an enclosed space, so we use in.
We say in the kitchen but at home.
Fill in the preposition: Tokyo is the most populated city ___ the world.
After a superlative we normally use in with a place: the most populated city in the world.
Of is used with a group, as in the best of all.
For addition of matrices, what must both matrices have?
The same order (same number of rows and columns)
The same number of columns only
Matrices are added element by element, so they must have the same number of rows and columns.
Matrix multiplication needs columns of the first to equal rows of the second.
Ziarat in Balochistan is known for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days in 1948.
Ziarat is also known for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.
For which religion is some area of Hassan Abdal sacred?
Hassan Abdal has Gurdwara Panja Sahib, which is sacred to Sikhs.
Panja Sahib is believed to hold a handprint of Guru Nanak on a boulder.
From where do plants mainly obtain nitrogen for growth?
Plants absorb nitrogen through their roots from the soil as nitrates and ammonium. Atmospheric nitrogen is made usable by bacteria and lightning.
Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules that fix nitrogen.
Where does the Yangtze River originate?
The Yangtze rises on the Tibetan Plateau in Qinghai and flows east to the East China Sea.
The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD?
Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany in 1908. He studied at Cambridge in England but his doctorate was from Munich.
His thesis was The Development of Metaphysics in Persia.
From which country does the TAPI gas pipeline start?
TAPI stands for Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and the gas comes from Turkmenistan.
The gas source is the Galkynysh field in Turkmenistan.
Mahatma Gandhi was a famous leader of which country?
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi led the Indian independence movement and the Indian National Congress.
Gandhi was assassinated in January 1948 in New Delhi.
From which province of China did the Corona (COVID-19) outbreak first begin?
The first cases were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, in December 2019.
WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020.
Hajj is which pillar of Islam?
The five pillars are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is the fifth.
Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who can afford it.
Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro belong to which civilization?
Both are major cities of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilization.
Mohenjo-Daro is in Sindh and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
Fill in the blank: She is always cleaning her home ___ cleanliness is called half faith.
The second clause gives the reason for her cleaning, so the conjunction because fits.
The saying Cleanliness is half of faith is attributed to the Prophet (PBUH).
Fill in the blank: The doctor ___ car makes noise is a good person.
Whose shows possession: the car belongs to the doctor.
Whose can be used for both people and things.
Fill in the blank: Why are you so ____ with him?
After the linking verb are, we need an adjective describing the subject, so angry.
Adverbs such as angrily describe verbs, not the subject after to be.
Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which companion?
Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), the first Caliph.
Her mother was Umm Ruman and she is known as Siddiqa bint Siddiq.
Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which clan (branch) of the Quraish tribe of Arabs?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish tribe. His grandfather was Abdul Muttalib, son of Hashim.
His father was Hazrat Abdullah and his mother was Hazrat Amina.
According to a hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), lying is a sign of which kind of person?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Sadiq (truthful) and Ameen (trustworthy) even before prophethood.
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of which Prophet?
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, and his son was Hazrat Yusuf (AS).
Choose the correct word: He is afraid ___ dogs.
The adjective afraid is followed by the preposition of, so the correct sentence is He is afraid of dogs.
Similar adjective-preposition pairs are fond of, proud of and afraid of.
Choose the correct word: He was born ___ 20 August 2001.
The preposition on is used with specific dates and days, so the sentence is He was born on 20 August 2001.
We use in for months and years (in August, in 2001) and at for clock times.
Hinda (Hind bint Utbah), wife of Abu Sufyan, embraced Islam after which event?
Hinda accepted Islam after the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH, when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) forgave the Makkans.
She was the mother of Hazrat Muawiya (RA) and had earlier opposed Muslims at Uhud.
Up to approximately what depth (in metres) does sunlight penetrate in the ocean (the sunlit or euphotic zone)?
Enough sunlight for photosynthesis reaches only to about 200 metres, which is called the sunlit (euphotic) zone.
Below it lies the twilight zone from about 200 m to 1000 m, and below 1000 m is the dark midnight zone.
How is the empty set denoted in set theory?
The empty set has no elements, so it is written as { } or with the symbol phi. The set {0} is not empty because it contains the element 0.
The empty set is a subset of every set and has zero elements.
What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line)?
The Durand Line, agreed in 1893, is most commonly given as about 2,640 km long.
Sources differ slightly (figures from about 2,600 to 2,670 km are quoted), and Afghanistan does not formally recognise the line.
How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan as of 2026?
The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and the 27th Amendment was passed by Parliament in November 2025. A 28th amendment was still only under discussion in mid-2026.
The 27th Amendment created the post of Chief of Defence Forces and a Federal Constitutional Court.
According to the Quran (Surah Al-Anfal), how many angels were promised by Allah to help the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
Surah Al-Anfal (8:9) says Allah would reinforce the Muslims with a thousand angels in succession.
Surah Al-Imran mentions 3000 and 5000 angels in other verses, and Muslims at Badr numbered 313.
According to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), how many countries are recognised as nuclear-weapon states?
The NPT recognises only the states that tested a nuclear device before 1 January 1967: USA, Russia, UK, France and China.
India, Pakistan and Israel never joined the NPT, and North Korea withdrew from it.
How many ayats (verses) are there in Surah Al-Kausar?
Surah Al-Kausar (Surah 108) has 3 ayats, which makes it the shortest surah of the Quran.
It begins with the words Inna a'taina kal-Kausar.
How many ayats were revealed in the first Wahi (revelation) in the Cave of Hira?
The first revelation consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra (Read).
The first Wahi came to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) through Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) in the month of Ramadan.
How many ayats does the shortest surah of the Quran contain?
The shortest surah is Al-Kausar, which has 3 ayats.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah, with 286 ayats.
How many books are included in the Sihah Sittah (Sahih Sitta), the six authentic collections of hadith?
Sihah Sittah literally means the six correct books. The six collections are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.
Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is regarded as the most authentic of them.
How many pieces of cloth are worn by a male pilgrim in the state of Ihram?
A male pilgrim wears two unstitched white sheets, one wrapped around the waist (izar) and one around the upper body (rida).
Women may wear their ordinary modest stitched clothes in Ihram.
How many consecutive matches did the Pakistani squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his famous unbeaten run?
Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986, until Ross Norman beat him in the 1986 World Open.
Some authors have questioned the exact count because records were poorly kept, but 555 is the figure officially cited.
How many countries have veto power in the United Nations Security Council?
Only the five permanent members have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
The Security Council also has 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms, who have no veto.
How many Hafiz (memorisers) of the Quran are reported to have been martyred in the Battle of Yamama?
In the Battle of Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailima, about 70 Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, according to the commonly given account.
Some narrations give higher numbers, but this event led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran in one book.
How many idols were placed in and around the Kaaba before the conquest of Makkah?
Traditional sources say 360 idols stood around the Kaaba when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah in 8 AH. He had them removed and the Kaaba cleansed.
The idol Hubal was the chief idol of the Quraysh inside the Kaaba.
How many books make up the Kutub-e-Sittah (the six authentic collections of Hadith)?
Kutub-e-Sittah literally means the six books: Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud, Jami Tirmidhi, Sunan Nasai and Sunan Ibn Majah.
Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is generally regarded as the most authentic of them.
How many Madani surahs does the Holy Quran contain, according to the common Pakistani textbook count?
Of the 114 surahs, 86 are Makki and 28 are Madani. Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrat.
Scholars differ slightly on a few surahs, so some books give slightly different counts.
How many manzils (stages) is the Holy Quran divided into?
The Quran is divided into seven manzils so that it can be recited in one week. Each manzil is read on one day of the week.
The Quran is also divided into 30 paras (juz).
How many masarif (heads of expenditure) of zakat are mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?

Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) names eight categories of zakat recipients: the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, the cause of Allah and the wayfarer.
Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.
What is the total number of members of the Senate of Pakistan?
The Senate has 96 members: 23 from each of the four provinces (92) plus 4 from the Islamabad Capital Territory. A November 2025 report still describes a 96-member Senate
The Senate had 104 members until the FATA seats were phased out after FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018.
How many Senate seats are allocated to each province of Pakistan?
Each province has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 for women, 4 for technocrats and 1 for non-Muslims.
The Senate is a permanent house; half of its members retire every three years.
How many general (directly elected) seats does Punjab have in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
Under the 2024 delimitation Punjab has 141 general seats in the 336-seat National Assembly. With its 32 reserved seats for women, Punjab's share rises to 173.
The National Assembly has 266 general seats, 60 for women and 10 for non-Muslims.
How many Nishan-e-Haider awards have been given so far, according to the commonly cited count?
The commonly cited current count is 11 recipients, all awarded posthumously. Older sources say 10, and the status of the eleventh name is sometimes disputed.
Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan.
How many nuclear-weapon states are recognised under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
The NPT recognises five nuclear-weapon states, those that tested before 1 January 1967: the USA, Russia, the UK, France and China. Pakistan, India, Israel and North Korea are outside this list.
The NPT came into force in 1970.
Into how many paras (juz) is the Holy Quran divided?
The Quran is divided into 30 paras of roughly equal length so it can be read in a month. This is separate from its 114 surahs.
The first para is Alif Lam Meem.
How many players are on the court for one team in a volleyball match?
A volleyball team has six players on the court at a time, three at the net and three at the back.
A basketball team has five players on court.
How many players of one team are on the court at a time in basketball?
Each basketball team plays with five players on the court at a time.
A team may have up to 12 players in total on its roster in international games.
Which rivers were allotted to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960, and how many are they?
Three western rivers: Indus, Jhelum and Chenab
Three eastern rivers: Ravi, Beas and Sutlej
The treaty gave Pakistan the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab). India received the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).
The treaty was brokered by the World Bank.
How many sides does a quadrilateral (such as a square) have?
A quadrilateral is a closed figure with four straight sides, and a square is a special case with four equal sides and four right angles.
The angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.
How many consecutive matches did squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his unbeaten run between 1981 and 1986?
Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches over about five and a half years, a record recognised in the Guinness Book of Records as the longest winning streak in a professional sport.
He won the British Open ten times in a row.
How many states are there in the United States of America?
The USA has 50 states. Alaska and Hawaii were the last to join in 1959.
Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.
How many surahs (chapters) are there in the Holy Quran?
The Holy Quran has 114 surahs, beginning with Al-Fatiha and ending with An-Nas.
86 surahs are Makki and 28 are Madani by the common count.
In which surah is the longest verse of the Holy Quran?
The longest verse is Ayat ad-Dayn (verse 282) about written contracts of debt, in Surah Al-Baqarah.
Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of the same surah.
Which is the shortest surah of the Holy Quran?
Surah Al-Kawthar has only three verses and the fewest words, so it is the shortest surah.
How many times does the full phrase Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem occur in the Holy Quran?
It opens 113 surahs (all except Surah At-Tawbah) and also appears inside Surah An-Naml (27:30), giving 114 in total.
Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
How many times is the name Muhammad mentioned in the Holy Quran?
The name Muhammad occurs in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:144), Al-Ahzab (33:40), Muhammad (47:2) and Al-Fath (48:29), so four times.
The name Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), appears once, in Surah As-Saff (61:6).
What is the Zakat nisab of silver in tolas?
The nisab of silver is 52.5 tolas, which is about 612.36 grams.
The nisab of gold is 7.5 tolas (about 87.48 grams), and the rate of Zakat is 2.5 percent.
How many types of Hajj are there?
The three types are Ifrad, Qiran and Tamattu.
Hajj-e-Tamattu is the type in which Umrah is done first and the Ihram is then removed before Hajj.
How many verses were revealed in the first Wahi (revelation) to the Holy Prophet (SAW) in the Cave of Hira?
The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq (Iqra bismi rabbikal-ladhi khalaq) were revealed first.
The revelation was brought by Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) in the Cave of Hira.
How often does the presidency of the UN Security Council change?
The presidency rotates every month among the 15 members in the English alphabetical order of their names.
The UN Security Council has 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
How old was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when his mother, Hazrat Amina, passed away?
Hazrat Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet (SAW) was about six years old.
His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then cared for him until he died when the Prophet (SAW) was eight.
Choose the correct word: I was worried because I thought I might ___ my train.
Miss means to fail to catch a train. Loose means not tight, and found is the past of find.
Lose (to misplace) and loose (not tight) are often confused.
ICAO is a specialized agency of which organization?
The International Civil Aviation Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations dealing with civil aviation standards.
ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
If A and B are disjoint sets, what is A intersection B?
Disjoint sets have no common element, so their intersection is the empty set.
The empty set is written as phi or { }.
What is the noun form of the adjective safe?
Safety is the noun that corresponds to the adjective safe, while safely is an adverb.
Many adjectives form nouns with the suffix -ty, such as certain and certainty.
From which city did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate in 622 AD?
In 622 AD the Prophet (SAW) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib), which is called the Hijrat.
The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.
If k is the unit vector along the z-axis, what is the scalar product k . k?
The dot product of a unit vector with itself is its magnitude squared, 1 x 1 = 1.
The dot product of two perpendicular unit vectors, such as i . j, is 0.
In the Quaid-e-Azam's 14 Points (1929), Sindh was to be separated from which province?
The 14 Points demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency and made a separate province.
Sindh actually became a separate province in 1936.
In the ratio a : b, what is a called?
The first term of a ratio is the antecedent and the second term is the consequent.
In the ratio 3 : 5, the antecedent is 3 and the consequent is 5.
In the sentence 'The boy ran into serious difficulties this year', which word is the adjective?
Serious describes the noun difficulties, so it is the adjective.
An adjective describes or qualifies a noun or pronoun.
In which battle were a large number of Hafiz-e-Quran Sahaba martyred?
Many Qurra (Hafiz) companions were martyred at Yamama against the false prophet Musaylima in 632 AD.
This loss led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to have the Quran compiled in one book.
In which battle was the tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) broken?
The Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded on the face during the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH, after the archers left their post.
The Battle of Uhud was fought near Madinah in March 625 CE.
In which para (juz) of the Holy Quran is Ayat ul Kursi found?
Ayat ul Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, and this verse falls in Para 3 (Tilka ar-Rusul).
Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, begins in Para 1 and ends in Para 3.
In which district of Balochistan is the Chamalang coal mine located?
The Chamalang coalfield lies in north-central Balochistan, mostly in Loralai district and extending towards Kohlu and Barkhan.
Some reports place the mine in the newly formed Duki district, which was carved out of Loralai; sources differ.
In which district of Pakistan is the Chashma nuclear power plant located?
The Chashma Nuclear Power Complex stands near Chashma barrage on the Indus in Mianwali district, Punjab.
Chashma Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was built with Chinese help.
In which city is the Cholistan Desert mainly located?
The Cholistan Desert (Rohi) lies in the Bahawalpur region of southern Punjab, bordering Rajasthan in India.
Cholistan is also known as the Rohi and is home to Derawar Fort.
In which city is Warsak Dam located?
Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River about 30 km north-west of Peshawar, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Warsak Dam was constructed in the 1960s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.
In which city is the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) situated?
PIMS is a large public teaching hospital located in sector G-8 of Islamabad.
Federal Government Polyclinic and PIMS are the main federal hospitals of Islamabad.
In which city of Pakistan does the Orange Line Metro Train run?
The Orange Line Metro Train is a rapid transit line in Lahore, built with Chinese financing under CPEC and opened in 2020.
It is Pakistan's first modern metro train system.
In which city was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
She was the first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country.
In which city was the Indian National Congress founded in 1885?
The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee.
A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, was the main founder of the Congress.
In which city did the tribes of Bani Aus and Bani Khazraj live?
Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later named Madinah, and they accepted Islam after the Pledges of Aqaba.
They are known as the Ansar (helpers) of Madinah.
In which country is the Gulf of Lion located?
The Gulf of Lion is a wide bay of the Mediterranean Sea off the southern coast of France.
Marseille and Montpellier are French cities near this coast.
In which country is the city of Wuhan located?
Wuhan is the capital of Hubei province in central China, on the Yangtze River.
Wuhan is also the city where the COVID-19 outbreak was first reported in December 2019.
In which country is the Suez Canal situated?
The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway running through Egypt.
It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and was opened in 1869.
Where was the first Olympic Games of ancient times held?
The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in Greece, traditionally dated to 776 BC.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
In which country was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) formed in 1969?
The OIC was founded at the Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969.
The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
To which land did the Muslims make their first migration (Hijrat) to escape persecution by the Quraish?
In the fifth year of the Prophethood a group of Muslims crossed the Red Sea to Abyssinia, whose Christian king Negus gave them protection.
Hazrat Usman and his wife Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) were among the first migrants.
In which district is Khanpur Dam located?
Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River near Khanpur town in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and was completed in 1983.
In which district is the Kharan Desert located?
The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of May 1998 at Chagai, a district near the Kharan Desert.
In which district is the hill station Gorakh Hill located?
Gorakh Hill, about 2,300 metres high, lies in the Kirthar Mountains of Dadu district, Sindh.
It is called the Murree of Sindh and sometimes receives snow in winter.
In which division is Narowal district?
Narowal district belongs to Lahore Division of Punjab.
Narowal was made a separate district in 1991 after being split from Sialkot.
In which mathematical equation does the expression b squared minus 4ac appear?
For ax squared + bx + c = 0, the quantity b squared minus 4ac is the discriminant under the square root of the quadratic formula.
If the discriminant is negative, the quadratic has no real roots.
For which achievement did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize in 2014?
She received the Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for the right of children and girls to education.
At 17 she is the youngest Nobel laureate in history and shared the prize with Kailash Satyarthi.
In which Ghazwa was Abu Jahal killed?
Abu Jahal, a leader of the Quraish, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH by the young Ansar brothers Muadh and Muawwidh.
He was fatally wounded by them and finished off by Abdullah bin Masud (RA).
In which Ghazwa did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) adopt the war technique of digging a trench around Madina?
On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) a trench was dug to defend Madina against the Quraish and allied tribes.
This battle is also called Ghazwa Ahzab.
In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa Ahzab (Khandaq) fought?
Most Pakistani textbooks place the Battle of the Trench in Shawwal 5 AH (627 CE).
Some historians place it in 4 AH, so sources differ.
In which Hijri year was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud, fought in Shawwal 3 AH.
He was killed by Wahshi and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.
In which Hijri year was the Battle of Yarmouk fought?
The Muslims defeated the Byzantines at Yarmouk in 15 AH (636 CE), in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).
The Muslim commander in this battle was Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).
In which Islamic month did Pakistan gain independence on 14 August 1947?
Pakistan came into being on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, which was 14 August 1947, a Friday.
27 Ramadan is also known as Laylat al-Qadr in popular belief.
In which Islamic month did the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhad take place?
The Battle of Uhad was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH near Mount Uhad close to Madina.
The Battle of Badr was fought in the previous year, in Ramadan 2 AH.
In which Islamic month did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
Imam Hussain (RA) was martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH, the day of Ashura.
The year of the event, 61 AH, fell during the rule of Yazid.
In which Islamic month is Eid ul Fitr celebrated?
Eid ul Fitr is celebrated on 1 Shawwal after the month of fasting ends.
Eid ul Fitr was first celebrated in 2 AH.
In which Islamic month is Laylat ul Qadr (the Night of Power)?
Laylat ul Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd nights.
Surah Al-Qadr is devoted to this night, which is described as better than a thousand months.
In which Islamic month was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
It is called Yaum ul Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
In which mountain range of Pakistan is Tirich Mir located?
Tirich Mir lies in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, in the Hindu Kush range.
At about 7,708 metres it is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.
In which Nabawi year did the Year of Grief (Aam ul Huzn) occur?
In the 10th year of prophethood both Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadijah (RA) passed away within a short time.
The year corresponds to about 619 CE.
In which province is Chagai district situated?
Chagai is a district in the west of Balochistan bordering Afghanistan and Iran.
Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai in May 1998.
In which province is the Gomal Zam Dam located?
Gomal Zam Dam is built on the Gomal River in South Waziristan, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is a multipurpose dam completed in 2013.
In which province of Pakistan is Ghotki located?
Ghotki is a city and district in northern Sindh, on the border with Punjab.
Ghotki lies on the Indus highway between Sukkur and Rahim Yar Khan.
In which province is Kundol (Kundal) Lake situated?
Kundol Lake lies in the upper Swat valley near Kalam in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Swat is famous for lakes such as Mahodand and Kundol.
In which part of Pakistan is Mirpur located?
Mirpur is a city and district in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (the question is often worded as province, though AJK is not a province).
Mangla Dam is built near Mirpur on the Jhelum River.
In which province is Narowal district located?
Narowal is a district in northeastern Punjab near the Indian border.
Narowal was made a separate district in 1991.
In which province does the Soan River flow?
The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar plateau of Punjab (Rawalpindi area) to join the Indus.
The Soan valley is one of the oldest sites of early human tools in South Asia.
On which river are the Victoria Falls situated?
Victoria Falls lies on the Zambezi River on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Its local name is Mosi-oa-Tunya, the smoke that thunders.
In which Surah does the phrase Bismillah occur twice (once at the start and once within a verse)?
In Surah Al-Naml the Bismillah appears at the start and again in verse 30 in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.
Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah without Bismillah at its start.
In which Surah was the first revelation to the Holy Prophet (SAW) revealed?
The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq were revealed in the cave of Hira, beginning with Iqra.
The revelation came in Ramadan when the Prophet (SAW) was 40 years old.
In which year did Britain annex Sindh?
Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani in 1843 and Sindh was annexed.
In which year did Hazrat Hind (wife of Abu Sufyan) embrace Islam?
She accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE).
She was the mother of Hazrat Muawiyah (RA).
In which year did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
Malala was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Kailash Satyarthi.
At age 17 she became the youngest Nobel laureate ever.
In which year did Pakistan become a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
Pakistan (with India) was admitted as a full member at the SCO summit in Astana, Kazakhstan, in June 2017.
Pakistan had been an SCO observer since 2005.
In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Cricket World Cup?
Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand under Imran Khan, beating England in the final at Melbourne.
It remains Pakistan's only 50-over World Cup title.
In which year did Pakistan last win the Hockey World Cup?
Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994, the last of these in Sydney in 1994.
Pakistan is the most successful team in World Cup history along with the Netherlands, with four titles each.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah die?
Jinnah died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, about thirteen months after Pakistan came into being.
He is buried at the Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.
In which year was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in Pakistan?
The Pakistan Army launched Radd-ul-Fasaad in February 2017 as a nationwide intelligence-based operation against terrorism.
It followed Operation Zarb-e-Azb, which began in June 2014.
In which year was the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia founded (unified) under Abdulaziz Ibn Saud?
Abdulaziz Ibn Saud proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932, which is marked as Saudi National Day.
Before that his realm was known as the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd.
In which year did the first Muslim commander, Muhammad bin Qasim, invade India (Sindh)?
Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 AD.
Some sources give 711 AD for his arrival; most Pakistani textbooks give 712 AD.
In which year did the Ottoman Empire come to an end?
The Ottoman Sultanate was abolished in November 1922, ending the empire, and Turkey became a republic in 1923.
The Caliphate was abolished separately on 3 March 1924 by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
In which year did the United Nations come into being?
The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding members.
United Nations Day is observed every year on 24 October.
In which year did the USA invade Afghanistan?
US-led forces began strikes on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.
The US withdrawal from Afghanistan was completed in August 2021.
From which year does the Islamic (Hijri) calendar start?
The Hijri calendar counts from the Prophet's migration (Hijrat) from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD.
It was introduced by Caliph Umar (RA) around 17 AH.
In which year was the M.A.O. School at Aligarh raised to the status of a College?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the school in 1875, and it became Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877.
The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
In which year was Tarbela Dam completed?
Construction of Tarbela Dam on the Indus began in 1968 and the dam was completed in 1976.
Sources differ: civil works finished around 1974 and the full power project in 1984; 1976 is the usual textbook answer.
In which year was the war of independence (the Mutiny) fought in the subcontinent?
The War of Independence broke out at Meerut in May 1857 against East India Company rule.
It ended with the British Crown taking direct control of India in 1858.
In which year were the modern Olympic Games first held?
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Baron Pierre de Coubertin revived the Games.
The International Olympic Committee was founded in 1894.
In which year was the Pakistan Resolution passed?
The Resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League on 23 March 1940.
It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.
In which year was the presidential system introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan under a new constitution?
Ayub Khan's constitution of 1962 introduced a presidential system with Basic Democracies.
The 1962 constitution was abrogated by Yahya Khan in 1969.
In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, taken as 570 AD in Pakistani textbooks.
In which year were the first Commonwealth Games (then called the British Empire Games) held?
The first British Empire Games were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. They were later renamed the Commonwealth Games.
The Games are held every four years and were named the British Commonwealth Games in 1970 and the Commonwealth Games in 1978.
In the straight line equation y = mx + c, what does m represent?
In y = mx + c, m is the slope (gradient) of the line, the change in y per unit change in x.
The constant c is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.
Is a Pakistan Navy Lieutenant equal in rank to a Pakistan Army Captain?
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Major
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Lieutenant
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Colonel
A Navy Lieutenant ranks with an Army Captain and a Pakistan Air Force Flight Lieutenant.
A Navy Lieutenant Commander is equal to an Army Major.
What is the shape of the graph of a quadratic equation?
The graph of y = ax^2 + bx + c with a not zero is a parabola.
The parabola opens upward if a is positive and downward if a is negative.
What is the status of Iran in SAARC?
SAARC has eight full members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Iran is only an observer, so it is not a member.
Other SAARC observers include China, Japan, the USA, the European Union, Australia, South Korea, Mauritius and Myanmar.
Is the number pi a rational or an irrational number?
Pi cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its decimal expansion never ends or repeats. Hence it is irrational.
Fractions such as 22/7 are only approximations of pi (3.14159...).
Joe Biden, who took office in January 2021, was which President of the USA?
Barack Obama was 44th and Donald Trump 45th, so Joe Biden who followed him was the 46th President.
Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 as the 47th President.
K2 lies on the border between Pakistan and which country?
K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) and Xinjiang (China).
K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8,611 m.
Lack of vitamin D causes which disease in the body?
Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones. Its deficiency causes rickets in children and soft bones in adults.
Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D.
Lapels are a part of which garment?
A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a coat or jacket below the collar.
The lapel is the part where a flower or badge is often pinned.
The rank of Lieutenant in the Pakistan Navy is equal to which rank in the Army?
Navy Sub Lieutenant equals Army Lieutenant, and Navy Lieutenant equals Army Captain.
Navy Lieutenant Commander equals Army Major.
Matrix A is of order 2 x 1 and matrix B is of order 1 x 2. What is the order of the product AB?
For a product the columns of A (1) equal the rows of B (1), so AB exists. Its order is rows of A by columns of B, that is 2 x 2.
The product BA in this case would be of order 1 x 1.
Narendra Modi is a famous politician of which country?
Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister of India, leading the BJP.
He has been Prime Minister since 2014 and is in his third term after the 2024 election.
Mohenjo-daro is located near which city of Sindh?
Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, lies in Larkana District on the right bank of the Indus.
Mohenjo-daro means Mound of the Dead and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Musailma Kazzab was killed in which battle?
Musailma, the false claimant of prophethood, was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Yamama in 632-633 CE in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.
Nanga Parbat is which highest peak of the world?
Nanga Parbat, at 8,126 m, is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
It is the second highest peak in Pakistan after K2 and is nicknamed Killer Mountain.
Nelson Mandela was the leader and later President of which country?
Mandela led the struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black President in 1994.
He was imprisoned for 27 years and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.
Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
Vitamin A is needed to form the visual pigment in the eye, so its lack makes it hard to see in dim light.
Carrots, spinach and liver are good sources of vitamin A.
Nuku'alofa is the capital of which country?
Nuku'alofa, on the island of Tongatapu, is the capital of the Kingdom of Tonga in the Pacific.
Tonga is a Polynesian monarchy and has never been fully colonised.
On what date did Pakistan get its first constitution?
Pakistan's first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and the country became an Islamic Republic.
It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law on 7 October 1958 and 23 March is now Pakistan Day.
On what date was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
She was killed in a gun and bomb attack after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country.
The Simla Conference of 1945 was held on 25 June 1945 under which Viceroy?
Viceroy Lord Wavell called the conference at Simla to discuss his plan for an Executive Council with Indian members.
It failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over the choice of Muslim members.
On what date was the State Bank of Pakistan established?
The State Bank of Pakistan began working on 1 July 1948 and was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam.
Its first Governor was Zahid Hussain.
On what date did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points, and in reply to which report?
28 March 1929, reply to the Nehru Report
23 March 1940, reply to the Cripps Mission
28 March 1929, reply to the Simon Report
12 December 1930, reply to the Lahore Resolution
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented his 14 Points in Delhi on 28 March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report of 1928.
The 14 Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, including separate electorates and one-third seats in the central legislature.
On which date of the Hijri month was the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (SAW) delivered?
The sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH, in the Uranah valley of Mount Arafat during the Farewell Hajj.
Some people say 10th, but the standard account is the Day of Arafah, the 9th.
On which date was SAARC formed?
SAARC was established at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985 by seven South Asian countries.
Its secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined in 2007.
According to the Quran, on which mountain did the ark of Prophet Noah (AS) come to rest?
Surah Hud (verse 44) says the ark settled on Al-Judi, a mountain in the Kurdistan region.
The Bible names the mountains of Ararat, so sources differ.
Canada and the United States are separated mostly by which parallel of latitude?
A large part of the border between Canada and the contiguous USA follows the 49th parallel north.
The 38th parallel divides North and South Korea.
On which Prophet was the Injil revealed?
The Injil (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (AS), known as Jesus.
The Zaboor was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (AS).
On which prophet was the Torah (Taurat) revealed?
The Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS) for the Bani Israil.
The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS), the Injeel on Hazrat Isa (AS) and the Quran on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
On which river is the Mirani Dam built?
Mirani Dam is built on the Dasht River in Kech district of Balochistan, near Turbat.
It was completed in 2006 mainly for irrigation and flood control in Makran.
On which river is Sukkur Barrage built?
Sukkur Barrage was built across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh.
It was opened in 1932 and feeds seven major canals.
On which river is Tarbela Dam built?
Tarbela Dam is an earth-filled dam on the Indus River in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world, completed in 1974.
On whom was the Zaboor (Psalms) revealed?
The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS).
Hazrat Dawud (AS) was also a king, and his son Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was a prophet too.
Pakistan is a gateway to which region?
Pakistan lies between South Asia, Central Asia and the Arabian Sea, so its ports and routes give Central Asia access to the sea.
Gwadar Port is promoted as a trade outlet for landlocked Central Asian states.
Pakistan is located in which continent?
Pakistan lies in South Asia, part of the continent of Asia.
Pakistan borders Afghanistan, China, India and Iran.
Who started Pakistan's biggest ambulance service?
Abdul Sattar Edhi founded the Edhi Foundation, which runs Pakistan's largest ambulance network.
Edhi is known as the Angel of Mercy and died in 2016.
Petrol is a mixture of what?
Petrol is a mixture of many liquid hydrocarbons obtained from crude oil.
Its octane number measures how well it resists knocking in an engine.
Ping pong is another name for which game?
Ping pong is the popular name for table tennis.
Table tennis has been an Olympic sport since 1988.
Pour le Merite is an award of which country?
Pour le Merite is a Prussian and German order of merit, first founded in 1740 by Frederick the Great.
In WWI the Blue Max was the nickname for its military class.
In which constitution of Pakistan was the presidential form of government adopted?
The 1962 constitution given by Ayub Khan established a presidential system with a strong president.
The 1956 and 1973 constitutions set up a parliamentary system.
Panja Sahib at Hassan Abdal is a sacred place of which religion?
Gurdwara Panja Sahib at Hassan Abdal is holy to Sikhs, who believe Guru Nanak's handprint is on a rock there.
Hassan Abdal is in Attock district, Punjab.
Which countries does the 38th parallel divide?
The 38th parallel north was the dividing line between North and South Korea after 1945.
The present border, the Demilitarized Zone, was set by the 1953 armistice and runs near the 38th parallel.
Rooh Ullah (Ruhullah) is the title of which prophet?
Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, the Spirit of Allah, because he was born by Allah's command without a father.
Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) Khalilullah.
Rubber is obtained from which tree?
Natural rubber is made from latex tapped from the rubber tree, Hevea brasiliensis.
Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are leading rubber producers.
Ruh-ul-Qudus is the title of which angel?
Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.
Hazrat Jibreel (AS) is also called Ameen.
In which month is Shab-e-Qadr (Laylatul Qadr)?
Laylatul Qadr falls in Ramadan, most likely on an odd night of the last ten days.
The Quran was first revealed on this night, and Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.
Complete the sentence: She said that she ___ to know.
In reported speech with the past tense verb said, the verb shifts to the past, so wanted is used.
This shifting of tense is called backshift.
Sound travels in the form of what?
Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs a medium such as air to travel.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Stainless steel is an example of what?
Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium and often nickel.
Chromium of at least about 10.5 percent makes it resist rust.
Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between Pakistan and India?
The Soviet Union under Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.
Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent soon after signing.
The Thar desert of Sindh is rich in which mineral resource?
Thar has one of the world's largest lignite coal reserves, about 175 billion tonnes.
Thar coal is being used for power generation at Islamkot.
The Battle of Furqan is the name of which ghazwa?
The Quran calls the day of Badr Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction between truth and falsehood. So the Battle of Furqan is the Battle of Badr.
Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) and about 313 Muslims faced roughly 1000 Makkan soldiers.
The census of Pakistan is conducted by which organization?
Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. NADRA and the Election Commission only use the data or registers.
The 2017 and the digital 2023 censuses were both conducted by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.
The Dorah Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Dorah Pass lies on the Chitral border and leads from Pakistan into Afghanistan (Badakhshan).
Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the Pakistani side of the Dorah Pass.
The first 5 verses revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong to which surah?
The first five ayats revealed in the Cave of Hira begin with Iqra bismi rabbika and are from Surah Al-Alaq.
Surah Al-Alaq is also called Surah Iqra.
The Hindukush range connects Pakistan with which country?
The Hindukush mountains run along the north-western border of Pakistan and extend into Afghanistan.
Tirich Mir (7708 m) in the Hindukush is the highest peak of the range in Pakistan.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of which place?
The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal to Yemen as governor and teacher of the people.
Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal was known as the most knowledgeable of the Companions in halal and haram.
The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 was made with the mediation of which organization?
The treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi in September 1960.
India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan rejects this move.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan has rights over which rivers?
The three western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab were allotted to Pakistan. The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej were given to India.
Pakistan and India agreed on the treaty after the Indus basin water dispute that followed Partition.
The nation of which prophet was destroyed by a rain of stones?
The Quran says the sinful people of Hazrat Loot (AS) were destroyed by a shower of baked clay stones.
The nation of Hazrat Nooh (AS) was destroyed by flood and the people of Aad by a violent wind.
The OIC is an organization of which countries?
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is the collective voice of Muslim countries of the world.
The OIC was founded in 1969 in Rabat and its headquarters are in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
The Panama Canal connects the Pacific Ocean with which ocean?
The canal cuts across Panama and joins the Pacific Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean through the Caribbean Sea.
The Panama Canal was opened in 1914 while the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is bound to act on the advice of whom?
Article 48 of the Constitution requires the President to act on the advice of the Prime Minister (or the Cabinet).
Pakistan has a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the real executive head.
The river Amazon is ___ largest river of South America.
A superlative such as largest takes the definite article the.
The Amazon is the largest river in the world by volume of water.
The rouble is the currency of which country?
The Russian rouble is the national currency of Russia.
Belarus also uses a currency called the Belarusian ruble.
The Secretary-General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, belongs to which country?
Antonio Guterres, the ninth UN Secretary-General, is a former Prime Minister of Portugal.
His term ends on 31 December 2026 and the selection of his successor is under way; before him Ban Ki-moon of South Korea held the post.
The Silk Road connects Pakistan with which country?
The Karakoram Highway follows part of the ancient Silk Road and links Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass.
The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is a modern project built along this old route.
The T.A.P.I gas pipeline starts from which country?
TAPI stands for Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and the gas comes from Turkmenistan (Galkynysh field).
The pipeline is planned to carry about 33 billion cubic metres of gas a year.
Choose the correct reported speech: The teacher asked, Who is speaking English?
The teacher wanted to know who is speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who was speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who has spoken English.
The teacher wanted to know who speaks English was.
In reported speech a present continuous question changes to past continuous, so is speaking becomes was speaking, and the question order becomes a statement.
The reporting verb asked is usually changed to wanted to know or enquired.
The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from which country?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan on the south and Tajikistan on the north.
The corridor also touches China at its eastern end.
The word Everyone is what part of speech?
Everyone stands in place of a noun (all people), so it is an indefinite pronoun.
Other indefinite pronouns are someone, anybody and nobody.
Thimphu is the capital of which country?
Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
Bhutan is a Himalayan kingdom between China and India.
Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Cancer not pass?
The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees north) crosses India, Bangladesh and Egypt, but Pakistan lies north of it.
It also passes through Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Libya and southern China.
Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Capricorn not pass?
The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 degrees south) lies in the southern hemisphere, and India is entirely in the northern hemisphere.
It also crosses Chile, Argentina, Namibia, Botswana and Madagascar.
To where did the Muslims first migrate?
In 615 CE (5th year of the Prophethood) a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia to escape persecution in Makkah.
The king of Abyssinia, Negus (Najashi), gave them protection.
To which country does Olympic Airlines (now Olympic Air) belong?
Olympic Airlines was the national flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis. It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009.
Olympic Airways was nationalised in 1975 and ceased operating as the flag carrier in 2009.
To which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib). This migration is the Hijrat.
The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.
To which tribe did Hazrat Ali (RA) belong?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in Makkah into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. He was the cousin of the Prophet (PBUH).
Aws and Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina.
With which wife of the Prophet (PBUH) was the compiled copy of the Quran kept after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected?

Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Quran compiled in book form; it passed to Hazrat Umar (RA) and then was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA), the Prophet's wife. Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare copies.
Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) led the compilation team under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
To whom is the title Zunnurain (possessor of two lights) given?
Hazrat Usman (RA) married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA), so he is called Zunnurain.
Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Caliph of Islam.
Two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) were married one after the other to which Sahabi?
Hazrat Ruqayyah and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) were both married to Hazrat Usman (RA).
Hazrat Fatima (RA), the youngest daughter, was married to Hazrat Ali (RA).
Umm Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) was what of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
She married Hazrat Usman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).
Towards which place was the first Hijrat of the Muslims made?
In 615 AD a small group of Muslims migrated from Makkah to Habsha (Abyssinia) to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Its Christian king, the Negus, gave them protection.
The migration to Madina came about seven years later, in 622 AD.
To whom was the Nishan-e-Haider last awarded?
Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed received the award for gallantry in the 1999 Kargil conflict; no later award is recorded.
Lalak Jan belonged to Yasin valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and is the 11th recipient.
Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan and the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, to India.
The treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 and mediated by the World Bank.
Under which organization is Pakistan's population census conducted?
Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS).
The latest census was the first fully digital one, held in 2023.
According to the 2023 census, Urdu is the mother tongue of about what percentage of Pakistanis?
The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics 2023 census puts Urdu at about 9.25 percent of the population. Candidates in 2021-22 recalled about 7 percent, which was the 2017 census figure (7.08 percent).
Punjabi is the most common mother tongue, at about 37 percent.
What are both houses of the Parliament of Pakistan (Senate and National Assembly) together called?
Under the 1973 Constitution the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora, consists of the President, the Senate and the National Assembly.
The Senate is the upper house and the National Assembly is the lower house.
Which are the three largest oceans of the world, in order of size?
By area the Pacific is the largest, then the Atlantic, then the Indian Ocean. The Southern and Arctic Oceans are smaller.
The Pacific Ocean covers about one third of the Earth's surface.
Which day is celebrated on 12 June?
The International Labour Organization observes the World Day Against Child Labour on 12 June each year.
World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Population Day on 11 July.
Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent electric light bulb in 1879. He also invented the phonograph.
The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
What does the word Al-Fatiha mean?
Al-Fatiha means The Opening, because it opens the Quran and also opens the prayer.
It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and has seven verses.
What does the Arabic word Ansar mean?
Ansar means helpers. It refers to the people of Madina who sheltered and helped the Muslims migrating from Makkah.
The migrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.
What does the Arabic word Badr (Badar) mean?
Badr means the full moon in Arabic. The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought at a place of that name near Madina.
The Battle of Badr was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.
Uhad (Uhud) is the name of what?
Uhud is a mountain just north of Madina, near which the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.
What does the word alter mean?
To alter something means to change it, usually slightly.
Alter is a verb; its related noun is alteration.
A pre-Islamic pact in Makkah to protect the oppressed and uphold justice
A treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraish in 6 AH
A pact made by the Ansar of Madinah at Aqabah
A trade agreement between Makkah and Syria
Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pledge made by several Makkan clans to help victims of injustice and to see that wrongs were set right. The Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that even after Islam he would respond to a similar call.
What does the term Ijtehad mean in Islamic law?
Independent reasoning to derive rulings from the Quran and Sunnah
Migration for the sake of faith
Ijtehad means exerting one's utmost intellectual effort to find a legal ruling on a new matter from the Quran and Sunnah. A scholar who does this is called a Mujtahid.
Allama Iqbal strongly advocated Ijtehad as the principle of movement in Islam.
What does the Arabic word Mantiq mean?
Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, the science of correct reasoning. It is taught in Dars-e-Nizami madrassas.
Muslim philosophers such as Al-Farabi and Ibn Sina wrote extensively on Mantiq.
What does NFC stand for in Pakistan's finance system?
NFC stands for National Finance Commission. It decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federation and the provinces.
The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.
What is 28 May, the day Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998, known as?
On 28 May 1998 Pakistan carried out nuclear tests at Chagai, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer. Takbeer means proclaiming the greatness of God.
Pakistan became the seventh nuclear power and the first Muslim nuclear state.
What does the abbreviation PSL stand for in Pakistani cricket?
PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the franchise Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan. It began in 2016.
The PSL is run by the Pakistan Cricket Board.
What does the word Pakistan mean?
Pakistan is a Persian and Urdu word made of pak (pure) and stan (land), so it means land of the pure. It is not related to truth.
The name was proposed by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
What does the word seething mean?
To seethe is to boil or churn, and it is used for a person who is extremely angry but does not show it. So seething means very angry.
Its literal meaning is bubbling as a liquid does when boiling.
Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
Tayammum is a substitute for wudu or ghusl performed with clean earth or dust when water is not available or cannot be used. It is taught in the Quran in Surah Al-Maidah.
Tayammum is made by striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face and hands.
What does the Silk Route connect?
China with the Mediterranean and Europe
The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade roads linking China through Central Asia to the Mediterranean world. Silk was a major good carried along it.
The Karakoram Highway in Pakistan follows part of the old Silk Route.
What does the word Akhuwat mean?
Akhuwat is an Arabic and Urdu word meaning brotherhood. It is the name of a Pakistani organisation that gives interest-free loans.
The Akhuwat concept is based on the brotherhood between the Muhajirin and the Ansar of Madinah.
What does the word Quran literally mean?
That which is recited or read
Quran comes from the Arabic root q-r-a, meaning to read or recite, so it literally means the recitation. It is the name of the holy book of Muslims.
The first revelation to the Prophet (PBUH) began with the command Iqra, meaning read.
Wuzu is the ritual ablution in which the face, arms, head and feet are washed or wiped before prayer. It is a condition for offering Salah.
Wuzu comes from an Arabic word connected with cleanliness and brightness.
What important event took place in 622 AD?
The Hijrah (migration) of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah
The Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD. This year marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?
By definition 0! = 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange no objects. This also keeps the formula n! = n x (n-1)! true for n = 1.
The number of ways to choose 0 items from n, nC0, equals 1 for this reason.
What is a period of 100 years also called?
A century is a period of 100 years. A decade is 10 years and a millennium is 1000 years.
A score means 20 years or 20 items.
What is 22 March observed as worldwide?
The United Nations observes 22 March each year as World Water Day. It raises awareness of fresh water and its sustainable use.
World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Health Day on 7 April.
What does the United Nations observe on 24 January?
The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January as International Day of Education in December 2018. It was first observed in 2019.
International Literacy Day is on 8 September and World Teachers Day on 5 October.
