The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.
What is an angle of 90 degrees called?
An angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle. Acute angles are smaller and obtuse angles are larger.
What was the relation of A. O. Hume with the Indian National Congress?
He was one of its founders in 1885
He was its first Muslim president
He was the Viceroy who banned it
Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the Indian National Congress in December 1885. He served as its first general secretary.
The first president of the Congress was W. C. Bonnerjee.
Which word is a synonym of alter?
To alter means to make something different, which is the same as to change it. The other options mean the opposite.
The noun form of alter is alteration.
Which word is a synonym of complicated?
Complicated means made of many parts and hard to understand, which is the meaning of complex. Simple, easy and plain are its opposites.
The opposite of complicated is simple.
Which word is a synonym of conceal?
To conceal means to keep something out of sight, which is to hide it. Reveal, show and expose are antonyms.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'dormant'?
Dormant means temporarily inactive or sleeping, as in a dormant volcano.
The opposite of dormant is active.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'evacuate'?
To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, especially because of danger.
Evacuate comes from the Latin word vacuare, meaning to empty.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'exquisite'?
Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful and finely made.
Its opposite could be crude or coarse.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'persistent'?
Persistent means continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is what tenacious means.
Persistent is the antonym of giving up or wavering.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'savage'?
Savage means fierce, wild and untamed.
Savage comes from the Latin silvaticus, meaning of the woods.
What is the closest meaning of the word voyage?
A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space. Journey is the closest meaning.
The word voyage comes from Old French voiage.
What is a zero vector also called?
A vector with zero magnitude and no definite direction is called a null vector.
Adding a null vector to any vector leaves it unchanged.
What is the abscissa of a point in the Cartesian plane?
In a point (x, y), the abscissa is the x-coordinate, the horizontal distance from the y-axis.
The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
Another name for the Manila Pact of 1954 is:
The Manila Pact created the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO), signed in Manila in September 1954.
What is Atomic Day (the day of Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests) called in Pakistan?
Pakistan tested nuclear devices in the Chagai hills in 1998, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.
It is observed on 28 May each year.
In statistics, what is the average of a set of numbers also called?
The average is the sum of the values divided by their count, which is the arithmetic mean.
The median is the middle value and the mode is the most frequent value.
Bait ul Muqaddas means the Holy House and refers to Jerusalem and its Masjid al-Aqsa.
It was the first Qibla of Muslims before the change to the Kaaba.
What is Barzakh in Islamic belief?
The period between death and the Day of Judgement
Barzakh is the barrier or intermediate state between a person's death and resurrection.
Barzakh is mentioned in Surah Al-Mu'minun of the Quran.
Which event is commemorated on Kashmir Day (Youm-e-Yakjehti-e-Kashmir) in Pakistan?
Solidarity with the people of Kashmir
Kashmir Day is observed to express support for the Kashmiri right to self-determination.
It is observed on 5 February each year.
What is cot x . sec x equal to?
cot x = cos x / sin x and sec x = 1 / cos x, so the product = 1 / sin x = cosec x.
Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.
What is the number of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first Rightly Guided Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH).
The order is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali (RA).
A peace pact of Makkan tribes to protect the oppressed
A treaty between Muslims and Jews of Madinah
Hilful Fudul was a pact formed in Makkah to defend the wronged and help the weak, and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it.
The Prophet (PBUH) later said he would still respond to such a pact in Islam.
In vector algebra, what is the value of j . j (dot product of the unit vector j with itself)?
Dot products of different unit vectors such as i . j are 0.
By what title is Liaquat Ali Khan known?
Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister, is called Quaid-e-Millat (leader of the nation).
Quaid-e-Azam is the title of Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
What is Pakistan Standard Time relative to UTC?
Pakistan Standard Time (PST) is five hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.
Among Muslim-majority countries, what is Pakistan's rank by population?
Indonesia has the largest population among Muslim-majority countries and Pakistan is second.
What is ping pong also called?
Ping pong is the popular name of table tennis.
Table tennis became an Olympic sport in 1988.
Which is the most populous district of Punjab, Pakistan?
Lahore has the largest population of any district in Punjab (about 13 million in the 2023 census).
Lahore is also the capital of Punjab.
What is a Ruku in the Holy Quran?
A section of verses marked in the text
A ruku in the Quran is a group of verses forming a section, marked with the letter ain in the margin.
In prayer, ruku also means bowing, but in the Mushaf it means a section.
SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area. It is a trade arrangement among the member states of SAARC to reduce customs duties.
SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006.
Sahih Muslim is a collection of authentic Hadith compiled by Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj.
Together with Sahih Bukhari it forms the Sahihain.
Stainless steel is mainly an alloy of iron with which metal?
Stainless steel is iron alloyed with at least about 10.5 percent chromium, which resists rust.
Nickel is often added as well.
What is the 15th night of Shaban called?
The night of the 15th of Shaban is known as Shab-e-Barat (night of forgiveness or record).
Shaban is the eighth month of the Islamic calendar and comes just before Ramadan.
Which is the 3rd surah of the Holy Quran?
The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Ali Imran, so the third is Ali Imran.
Surah Ali Imran has 200 verses and is a Madani surah.
In the commonly taught Pakistani order of the five pillars of Islam (Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat, Hajj), which is the 4th pillar?
In this order the pillars run Shahada, Salah, Fasting, Zakat, Hajj, so the fourth is Zakat.
Sources differ: the hadith in Sahih Bukhari lists Hajj before fasting, which makes Hajj fourth.
An acute angle is how large compared with a right angle?
A right angle is 90 degrees and an acute angle is any angle between 0 and 90 degrees, so it is smaller.
An angle larger than 90 and smaller than 180 degrees is called obtuse.
On which date is American Independence Day celebrated?
The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, and that day is celebrated as Independence Day.
The Declaration was mainly drafted by Thomas Jefferson.
An ally is a supporter or friend, and its opposite is an enemy or foe.
The word ally comes from the Latin alligare, meaning to bind to.
To cease means to stop, so its opposite is to continue.
Cease is also often used in the phrase ceasefire.
A chum is a close friend, and the opposite is an enemy.
Chum is an informal word and a synonym of buddy.
To climb is to go up, and the opposite is to descend (go down).
Descend comes from the Latin descendere.
Expansion means growing larger, and its opposite is contraction (becoming smaller).
In economics the opposite phases are expansion and contraction (recession).
To proceed is to go forward, and the opposite is to halt or stop.
Proceed is a synonym of advance, continue and progress.
Which line is the boundary between Pakistani Punjab and Indian Punjab?
The 1947 boundary award of Sir Cyril Radcliffe divided Punjab and Bengal between Pakistan and India.
The Durand Line separates Pakistan and Afghanistan, and the McMahon Line is in the India-China area.
Which name is given to the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) in the Quran?
The Battle of Khandaq (5 AH) is also called Ahzab (the Confederates), after the allied tribes who besieged Madinah.
The trench was dug on the advice of Salman al-Farsi.
What is the base of the natural logarithm?
The natural logarithm ln x is the logarithm to base e, where e is approximately 2.71828.
Common logarithms use base 10, and computer science often uses base 2.
What is the value of tan(-x)?
Tangent is an odd function, because sin(-x) = -sin x and cos(-x) = cos x, so tan(-x) = -tan x.
Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.
Which is the biggest continent in the world by area?
Asia covers about 44.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest of all continents.
Asia is also the most populous continent.
In Islam, which is the biggest sin?
The Quran and Hadith describe shirk as the greatest sin, and Allah does not forgive it unless a person repents.
The Quran (Surah An-Nisa 4:48) says that Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives lesser sins.
What is the capital of Balochistan?
Quetta is the provincial capital and largest city of Balochistan.
Quetta is known as the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.
What is the capital of Bangladesh?
Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.
Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in 1971.
What is the political capital of Burundi?
Burundi moved its political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.
Bujumbura remains the economic capital and the largest city, and was the capital before 2019.
What is the capital of Canada?
Ottawa is the capital of Canada, although Toronto is the largest city.
Ottawa lies on the Ottawa River in the province of Ontario.
What is the capital of Germany?
Berlin is the capital of Germany.
Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification in 1990.
What is the capital of Peru?
Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru.
Bogota is the capital of Colombia, Quito of Ecuador and Santiago of Chile.
What is the capital of Australia?
Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.
Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia and Yerevan of Armenia.
What is the capital of Uganda?
Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
Entebbe, near Kampala, hosts Uganda's main international airport.
Which city was the capital of the ancient Gandhara civilization in Pakistani textbooks?
Taxila (Takshashila) is the capital of Gandhara most often given in Pakistani textbooks.
Sources differ: Pushkalavati and later Peshawar (Purushapura) also served as Gandhara capitals.
What is the closest meaning of the word abundant?
Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the closest synonym.
The opposite of abundant is scarce.
What is the closest meaning of the word collaboration?
Collaboration means working together with others toward a common goal. Cooperation has the closest meaning.
The word collaborate comes from Latin meaning to labour together.
What is the closest meaning of the word compassion?
Compassion is a feeling of concern and pity for the suffering of others. Sympathy is the closest meaning.
Its opposite is cruelty or ruthlessness.
What is the closest meaning of the word extensive?
Extensive means covering a large area or having a wide range. Widespread is the closest meaning.
The opposite of extensive is limited.
What is the closest meaning of the word inhabitant?
An inhabitant is a person who lives permanently in a place. Resident has the same meaning.
The word comes from Latin inhabitare, meaning to dwell in.
What is the closest meaning of the word juvenile?
Juvenile refers to a young person or something belonging to young people. Youthful is the closest meaning.
A juvenile court deals with offenders below the adult age.
What is the closest meaning of the word slackness?
Slackness means lack of tightness, energy or care. Looseness or laziness fits best.
Slack is the opposite of taut.
What is the closest meaning of the word consent?
Consent means agreement or permission to do something.
The opposite of consent is dissent.
What is the special unstitched cloth worn by pilgrims during Hajj called?
Ihram is the two-piece unstitched white cloth worn by male pilgrims during Hajj and Umrah. Wearing it begins the state of ihram.
Women pilgrims wear ordinary modest clothing and do not wear a special unstitched sheet.
What is the combination of the upper house and lower house of a legislature called?
The legislature made up of the upper and lower houses is called Parliament. In Pakistan it is the Majlis-e-Shoora.
Pakistan's Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate together with the President.
The final consonant n is doubled when adding ing to begin, giving beginning.
Similar doubling occurs in running and swimming.
What is the currency of Belarus?
Belarus uses the Belarusian ruble (code BYN).
The hryvnia is the currency of Ukraine and the zloty that of Poland.
What is the currency of Kenya?
Kenya uses the Kenyan shilling (code KES).
Ethiopia uses the birr and South Africa the rand.
What is the currency of Libya?
Libya uses the Libyan dinar (code LYD).
The Libyan pound was replaced by the dinar in 1971.
What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (code LKR).
The taka is the currency of Bangladesh and the rufiyaa that of the Maldives.
What is the date of America's Independence Day?
The Declaration of Independence of the United States was adopted on 4 July 1776, which is celebrated as Independence Day.
Americans celebrate it every year on 4 July.
On what date did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah die?
Quaid-e-Azam died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, a little over a year after Pakistan was created.
His death anniversary is observed on 11 September every year.
In which month and Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah (Fatah Makkah) take place?
The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah with an army of about ten thousand in Ramadan 8 AH, traditionally dated 20 Ramadan.
The conquest took place almost without bloodshed and the Prophet (PBUH) granted a general amnesty.
On which date was the Battle of Uhud fought?
The Battle of Uhud was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE) near Mount Uhud, close to Madina.
Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in this battle.
On which date was the Battle of Badr fought?
The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraish.
It is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
On which date did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.
He was awarded Nishan-e-Imtiaz and Hilal-e-Imtiaz.
When did the Quaid-e-Azam present his famous Fourteen Points?
Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in Delhi in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
The Lahore Resolution came later, in March 1940.
What name is given to 28 May, the day Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in 1998?
Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998 and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.
Pakistan became the seventh declared nuclear power.
What is the derivative of the exponential function e to the power x with respect to x?
x times e to the power (x minus 1)
The function e^x is its own derivative, so d/dx of e^x equals e^x.
The derivative of a to the power x is a^x times ln a.
What is the term of a Senator in Pakistan?
Senators are elected for a six-year term, and half retire every three years.
The Senate itself is a permanent house and is never dissolved.
What is the duty of Hazrat Mikail (AS)?
Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and the provision of sustenance.
Hazrat Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Azrael takes souls.
What is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
The Hijri calendar begins with Muharram, and 1 Muharram is the Islamic New Year.
The calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from the Hijrah to Madina.
According to the Islamic teachings, which question is first asked from a person in the grave?
Munkar and Nakir first ask the deceased: Who is your Lord (Man Rabbuka)? Then they ask about his religion and his Prophet.
Salah is the first deed to be accounted for on the Day of Judgement.
On which date was the State Bank of Pakistan formally started?
The State Bank of Pakistan began functioning on 1 July 1948 and was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam.
Before it, the Reserve Bank of India handled central banking for Pakistan for a short time.
What is the full official name of Pakistan?
Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Pakistan was named an Islamic Republic for the first time in the Constitution of 1956.
What is the standard time offset of Pakistan from GMT (UTC)?
Pakistan Standard Time is five hours ahead of GMT, that is UTC+5.
India uses UTC+5:30, so Pakistan is 30 minutes behind India.
Which surah is called the heart (Qalb) of the Quran?
A hadith narrated in the books of Hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.
Surah Yaseen is the 36th surah and has 83 verses.
What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
Tirich Mir in Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, about 7,708 metres high.
Some Pakistani textbooks give 7,690 m, so sources differ slightly.
What is the highest court of Pakistan?
The Supreme Court of Pakistan, in Islamabad, is the apex court of the country.
The Federal Shariat Court examines whether laws conform to Islamic injunctions.
What is the highest power of the variable in a polynomial called?
The degree of a polynomial is the largest exponent of its variable. For example, x^3 + 2x has degree 3.
A polynomial of degree 2 is called a quadratic.
On which date is Independence Day of the USA celebrated?
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776.
The 4 July 1776 declaration separated the thirteen colonies from Britain.
What is the integral part of a logarithm called?
A logarithm has two parts: the integer part is the characteristic and the decimal part is the mantissa.
The mantissa of a common logarithm is always kept positive.
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is an agency of which organization?
ICAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that sets standards for international civil aviation.
ICAO was created by the 1944 Chicago Convention and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
Which Caliph of Islam is known by the title Zun-Noorain (possessor of two lights)?
Hazrat Usman bin Affan (RA) married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Ruqayyah and later Umm Kulthum, so he is called Zun-Noorain.
Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Caliph and is also called Ghani.
Which is the largest bone of the human body?
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
The smallest bone is the stapes in the middle ear.
Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population?
Karachi is the most populous city of Pakistan, with over 14 million people at the 2017 census and about 20 million at the 2023 census.
Lahore is the second largest city.
Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
The Sahara in North Africa covers about 9 million square kilometres and is the largest hot desert.
Counting cold deserts, Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
Which is the largest gulf in the world?
The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest gulf.
The Persian Gulf is much smaller, at about 250,000 square kilometres.
Which is the largest plateau of the world by area?
The Tibetan Plateau covers about 2.5 million square kilometres and is the largest as well as the highest plateau.
It is often called the Roof of the World.
Which is the largest sea of Europe?
The Mediterranean Sea covers about 2.5 million square kilometres, more than any other sea touching Europe.
The Mediterranean connects to the Atlantic Ocean through the Strait of Gibraltar.
What is the upgraded version of the Pakistani missile Hatf-IV (Shaheen-I) called?
Hatf-IV is the Shaheen-I ballistic missile, and its longer-range upgraded variant is called Shaheen-IA.
Shaheen-IA was first test fired in April 2012.
What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line)?
The Durand Line, drawn in 1893, forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan and is usually quoted as about 2,640 km long.
Sources differ slightly (about 2,600 to 2,670 km), and Afghanistan has long disputed the Durand Line as an international border.
What is the literal meaning of the word Furqan?
The criterion that separates right from wrong
Furqan comes from an Arabic root meaning to separate or distinguish. It therefore means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
Al-Furqan is a name of the Holy Quran and the title of the 25th surah.
What is the literal meaning of the word Islam?
Submission and surrender to the will of Allah
Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission, surrender and also peace. It means submitting oneself to Allah.
A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.
What is the literal meaning of Tayammum?
To intend or aim at something
Tayammum literally means to intend or to aim at something. In Islamic law it means purifying oneself with clean earth when water is unavailable.
Tayammum is allowed in place of wudu or ghusl when water is not available or its use would be harmful.
Which is the longest river of South America?
The Amazon, about 6,400 km long, is the longest river of South America and carries the largest volume of water in the world.
The Amazon flows mainly through Brazil and empties into the Atlantic Ocean.
By what other name is the Manila Pact of 1954 known?
The Manila Pact was signed in 1954 and created the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO).
Pakistan joined SEATO in 1954 and the alliance was dissolved in 1977.
What is the meaning of the word Al-Noor?
Noor is an Arabic word meaning light, and Al-Noor means The Light.
Surah An-Nur is the 24th surah of the Holy Quran and Al-Nur is one of the names of Allah.
What is the meaning of the word Ayat?
Ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign. It is used for the verses of the Holy Quran, which are signs of Allah.
Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
What is the meaning of the word conscious?
Conscious means being awake and aware of oneself or one's surroundings.
What is the meaning of the word exquisite?
Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful, finely made or carefully crafted.
It can also describe intense feelings, as in exquisite pleasure.
What is the meaning of the word gallant?
Gallant means brave and heroic, and also politely attentive to women.
Gallantry awards are given to soldiers for bravery in action.
What is the meaning of Hilf-ul-Fudul?
Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah by chiefs who promised to defend the oppressed and give justice to all. Its name means the pact of the virtuous.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man before prophethood and praised it later.
What is the meaning of the name Israel?
Israel is a Hebrew name, the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), meaning servant of God (Abdullah).
The descendants of Hazrat Yaqub (AS) are called Bani Israel.
What is the meaning of the word Mantiq?
Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, from a root meaning speech or reasoning.
Mantiq is a classic subject of the Islamic religious curriculum.
What is the meaning of the word oppression?
Cruel or unjust treatment of people
Oppression means the prolonged cruel or unjust use of power over others.
Zulm is the Urdu and Arabic word for oppression.
What is the meaning of the word Pakistan?
Pak means pure and stan means land, so Pakistan means land of the pure.
The name was coined by Choudhary Rahmat Ali in 1933.
What is the meaning of Ruku in prayer?
Ruku means to bow, and in salah it is the posture of bowing with hands on the knees.
Sajdah, the prostration, is the posture that follows ruku.
What is the meaning of the word Tanzeel?
Tanzeel comes from an Arabic root meaning to send down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.
The Quran says it is a Tanzeel from the Lord of the worlds.
What is the meaning of the word voyage?
A long journey, especially by sea
A voyage is a long journey, especially one made by sea or in space.
Bon voyage is a French phrase wishing someone a pleasant journey.
What is the meaning of Wudu (Wuzu)?
Ablution, the ritual washing before prayer
Wudu means ablution, the washing of the face, hands, head and feet before prayer, from a root meaning cleanliness.
In the Hanafi school wudu has four faraiz, as stated in Surah Al-Maidah.
What is the meaning of the word defer?
To defer means to put off something until a later time.
Another meaning is to yield to someone's opinion, as in defer to the elders.
What is the most abundant organic compound on Earth?
Cellulose forms the cell walls of plants and is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.
Which is the most populated city of Pakistan?
The 2023 census counted about 20.4 million people in Karachi division, ahead of Lahore with about 13 million.
Some candidates in 2021-22 wrote Lahore, but Karachi has always had the largest population.
Which currency is most used in world trade?
The US dollar is the main currency for invoicing trade and for global reserves.
The euro is the second most used reserve currency.
What is the multiplicative inverse of an identity matrix?
Since I times I equals I, the inverse of an identity matrix is the identity matrix itself.
Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.
Who was the father of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was his younger half-brother.
What is the boundary line between Pakistan and India in Kashmir called?
The Line of Control (LoC) separates Pakistan-administered and Indian-administered Kashmir.
It was established by the 1972 Simla Agreement, based on the 1949 ceasefire line.
Which continent is known as the Dark Continent?
Africa was called the Dark Continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans for a long time.
The nickname became popular through the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.
What was the name of the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) who was married to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What was the name of Pakistan's first satellite?
Badr-1, launched on 16 July 1990 from China, was the first satellite of Pakistan.
Which strait separates Russia and the United States (Alaska)?
The Bering Strait lies between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and Alaska in the United States.
It connects the Pacific and Arctic oceans and is about 85 km wide.
What is the national animal of Pakistan?
The Markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.
The Chukar partridge is the national bird, the Deodar the national tree and Jasmine the national flower of Pakistan.
Which word is nearest in meaning to 'diversity'?
Diversity means a range of different things, which is what variety means. Uniformity and similarity are its opposites.
Its adjective form is 'diverse', meaning varied or different in kind.
What is the new name of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD)?
RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
ECO has its secretariat in Tehran.
What is the nisab (minimum threshold) of gold for zakat, in tola?
The nisab of gold is 7.5 tola (about 87.48 grams). The 52.5 tola figure is the nisab of silver.
Zakat on wealth at or above the nisab is 2.5 percent.
What is the rate of ushr (zakat on agricultural produce) on land watered by rain?
Ushr means one tenth, so produce from rain-fed land is charged at 10 percent. Land irrigated at a cost is charged at half of that, 5 percent.
Ushr is due on the harvest itself rather than on yearly savings.
How many Madani surahs are there in the Quran?
The Quran has 114 surahs, of which 86 are Makki, so 114 minus 86 leaves 28 Madani surahs.
Sources differ slightly in classifying a few surahs, but 86 Makki and 28 Madani is the usual textbook count.
Savage means wild and uncivilized, so its opposite is civilized. Fierce, wild and brutal are similar in meaning to savage.
Savage can also be used as a noun for a brutal person.
Tame means domesticated and not dangerous, so its opposite is wild. Gentle, docile and domestic are close to tame in meaning.
Tame can also describe something dull, such as a tame film.
What is the period between a person's death and the Day of Judgment called in Islam?
Barzakh is the intermediate stage between death and resurrection, in which the soul stays until the Day of Judgment.
Barzakh is also the Quranic word for a barrier, for example between two seas in Surah Ar-Rahman.

A Muslim League report on the treatment of Muslims under Congress ministries
A report on the partition of Bengal

The Muslim League also observed a Day of Deliverance in December 1939 when the Congress ministries resigned.
What is the radian measure of a half circle (a straight angle)?
A full circle is 2 pi radians, so half of it is pi radians, which equals 180 degrees.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was related to Hazrat Abu Talib as his:
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), who raised Ali's cousin the Prophet.
Ali's mother was Fatima bint Asad, and his brother Jafar was also a son of Abu Talib.
What is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors A and B?
A B sin(theta) as a vector
The scalar product is A.B = |A||B|cos(theta), where theta is the angle between them. The result is a number, not a vector.
The vector (cross) product uses sin(theta) and gives a vector.
What is the other name of the Battle of Ahzab?
The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) is also called the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah. It was fought in 5 AH.
The trench was dug on the suggestion of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).
What is the shaving of the head during Hajj called?
Halq is shaving the whole head, and Qasr is trimming the hair. One of them is done to come out of the state of Ihram.
Women only trim a small portion of their hair (Taqsir).
Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
Vatican City covers about 0.44 square km, the smallest independent state in the world. Monaco is the second smallest.
Vatican City is an enclave inside the city of Rome, Italy.
What is the source of the Yellow River (Huang He)?
Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai, China
The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains of Qinghai Province, China. It then flows east into the Bohai Sea.
The river is about 5,464 km long, though sources differ on the exact figure.
Which word is closest in meaning to ADHERENT?
An adherent is a supporter or follower of a person, party or idea.
The verb adhere means to stick to or stay loyal to something.
Which word is closest in meaning to CONSENT?
Consent means permission or agreement to something.
Its opposite is dissent or refusal.
Which word is closest in meaning to DIVERSITY?
Diversity means a range of different things or people, which is variety.
Which word is closest in meaning to EXCITING?
Exciting means causing great enthusiasm or eagerness, which is thrilling.
The word excite comes from the Latin excitare, meaning to rouse.
Which word is closest in meaning to EXTREMELY?
Extremely means to a very high degree, which is exceedingly.
Words such as utterly and highly are also similar in sense.
Which word is closest in meaning to FLOURISH?
To flourish is to grow and develop in a healthy, successful way, which is to thrive.
Its opposite is to decay or wither.
Which word is closest in meaning to HERITAGE?
Heritage is what is passed down from earlier generations, such as traditions and property, which is a legacy.
UNESCO lists World Heritage Sites such as Moenjodaro and Taxila in Pakistan.
Which word is closest in meaning to HIERARCHY?
A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged in order of rank or importance.
The army rank structure is a typical hierarchy.
Which word is closest in meaning to IMPAIR?
To impair is to damage or weaken something so that it works less well. The candidate answer Ridicule has a different meaning.
Its opposite is to enhance or improve.
Which word is closest in meaning to INDIFFERENCE?
Indifference is a lack of interest or concern, which is apathy.
Its opposite is concern or enthusiasm.
Which word is closest in meaning to LAXITY?
Laxity means lack of strictness or care, which is slackness.
Its opposite is rigour or strictness.
Which word is closest in meaning to LEISURE?
Leisure is time free from work or duties, which is free time.
The word comes from the Old French leisir, meaning to be permitted.
Which word is closest in meaning to MALICIOUS?
Malicious means intending to harm others, which is spiteful.
Which word is closest in meaning to MEDIATE?
To mediate is to step in between two sides in a dispute to settle it, which is to arbitrate.
A mediator is a neutral person who helps two parties reach agreement.
Which word is closest in meaning to OPPRESS?
To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unjust use of power, which is to persecute.
Which word is closest in meaning to PRECEDING?
Preceding means coming before in time or order, which is previous.
Its opposite is succeeding or following.
Which word is closest in meaning to PREVENT?
To prevent is to stop something from happening, which is to avert.
Hinder and thwart are also close in meaning.
Which word is closest in meaning to PROMINENT?
Prominent means well known or important, which is eminent.
It can also mean easily seen or standing out.
Which word is closest in meaning to RESENTMENT?
Resentment is a feeling of bitter anger about unfair treatment, which is bitterness.
Which word is closest in meaning to SPLENDID?
Splendid means very impressive or excellent, which is magnificent.
Splendid comes from the Latin splendere, to shine.
Which word is closest in meaning to TIMID?
Timid means lacking courage or confidence, which is shy.
Its opposite is bold or daring.
Which word is closest in meaning to TOTALLY?
Totally means in every way or to the full extent, which is completely or entirely.
Utterly and wholly are other close words.
Which word is closest in meaning to TYRANT?
A tyrant is a ruler who uses power in a cruel and unjust way, which is a despot.
Its opposite in sense is a benevolent ruler.
Which is the tallest animal living on land?
An adult giraffe can reach about 5 to 5.5 metres in height. No other land animal is taller.
Giraffes mostly eat leaves from acacia trees.
What is the title (laqab) of Hazrat Adam (AS)?
Hazrat Adam (AS) is called Abul Bashar, the father of mankind. He is also called Safiullah.
He was the first human and the first prophet in Islamic belief.
What is the title of Hazrat Isa (AS)?
Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah) and also Al-Masih. Khalilullah is for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Zabihullah for Ismail (AS).
He was born miraculously to Hazrat Maryam (AS) without a father.
What is the title of Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is called Ruh ul Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit) in the Quran, and also Ruh ul Quds.
He brought revelation to all prophets, including the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
What is the length of the Line of Control (LoC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir in kilometres, as most commonly given?
The Line of Control was set after the 1971 war and the Simla Agreement of 1972. It is most commonly given as about 740 km.
Sources differ, with some giving up to 776 km.
How many bones are there in the adult human body?
An adult skeleton has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300 which fuse as the child grows.
The femur is the longest bone of the body.
How many landlocked countries are there in the world?
Counting internationally recognised sovereign states with no sea coastline gives 44 landlocked countries.
Counts differ slightly between sources (up to 49) when partially recognised states such as Kosovo are included.
How many Manzils (equal divisions for weekly recitation) is the Quran divided into?
The Quran is divided into 7 Manzils so that it can be completed in one week.
The Quran is also divided into 30 Paras (Juz).
What is the total number of seats of the Senate of Pakistan today?

Candidates in 2021-22 may have answered 104, which was the number before the reduction.
What is the upper house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
Pakistan's Parliament has two houses, and the upper house is the Senate.
The lower house is the National Assembly.
What is the rate of ushr on crops grown with artificial irrigation (tube wells, canals bought or built at cost)?
Ushr is 10 percent on rain-fed land and half of that, 5 percent, where artificial irrigation involves cost.
Zakat on gold, silver and cash is 2.5 percent.
What is the rate of zakat on gold and silver (above nisab)?
Zakat on gold, silver and cash savings above nisab is one-fortieth, which is 2.5 percent.
Nisab for gold is about 7.5 tola (87.48 grams) and for silver 52.5 tola.
Which is the world's most populous country today?
India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, according to the United Nations.
Before 2023 China was the most populous country.
What is the Yellow River of China also called?
The Yellow River is known in Chinese as the Huang He.
The Yangtze is the longest river in China and Asia.
Uhud is a mountain just north of Madinah where the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.
Youm-ul-Furqan is the name given to the day of which battle?
The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish.
Which major event took place in 8 Hijri?
Makkah was conquered peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
The Treaty of Hudaibiya was in 6 AH and the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
Which part of speech is the word 'ouch'?
'Ouch' expresses sudden pain or emotion, which is the job of an interjection.

Muslims dug a trench around the open northern side of Madinah to stop the Quraish cavalry.

What type of government system was set up by the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1973 Constitution created a federal parliamentary system with a Prime Minister as chief executive and a President as head of state.

What type of star is the Sun?
The Sun is a G2V main-sequence star, usually called a yellow dwarf.
In about five billion years it will become a red giant.
For what is Hakeem Luqman best known?
Luqman was a sage whose wisdom and advice to his son are praised in the Quran.
Surah Luqman (Surah 31) is named after him.
Regional Cooperation for Development among Pakistan, Iran and Turkey
Regional Council for Defence of Asia
Regional Cooperation for Defence among Muslim states

For what is Sher Shah Suri best known?
Grand Trade Road and administrative reforms

At what age did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
The first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) came in the cave of Hira when the Prophet was 40 years old.
He was born in 570 CE and the first revelation came in about 610 CE.
What was the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961?
A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba
A US naval battle with Japan

It was followed in 1962 by the Cuban Missile Crisis.

A 1946 plan for a united India

Which is considered the first book of Hadith compiled?
Imam Malik compiled the Muwatta in Madinah in the 8th century, and it is generally taken as the first book of Hadith.
Some sources mention earlier small collections such as Sahifa Hammam ibn Munabbih.
What was the name of the 1917 revolution in Russia (USSR) that overthrew the Tsarist system?
In 1917 the Bolsheviks led by Lenin seized power in Russia, ending Tsarist and provisional rule. It is known as the Bolshevik or October Revolution.
The USSR itself was formed in 1922 and dissolved in 1991.
How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
The Muslim army at Badr numbered about 313 men, against roughly 1000 Quraish soldiers.
Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
Which international organization was the predecessor of the United Nations (UNO)?
The League of Nations, founded in 1920 after World War I, failed to prevent World War II and was replaced by the UN in 1945.
The League of Nations was headquartered in Geneva.
What was the main purpose of Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched by Pakistan in 2017?
To eliminate residual and latent terrorism and consolidate earlier gains
To fight a war with India

Operation Zarb-e-Azb began in North Waziristan in June 2014.
What was the relation of Hazrat Umme Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA). She was married to Hazrat Uthman (RA) after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.

What was the relation of Hazrat Hafsa (RA) with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Hafsa (RA), daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA), married the Prophet (PBUH) and is a Mother of the Believers.

In which period did Hazrat Umar (RA) hold the caliphate?
Hazrat Umar (RA) became caliph after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) in 634 CE and was martyred in 644 CE, ruling about ten and a half years.

What title is associated with Liaquat Ali Khan?
Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, is known as Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951 and is also called Shaheed-e-Millat.
What was the Simla Conference of 1945?
A meeting of Wavell with Indian leaders on self-government that failed
The signing of the Pakistan-India peace agreement
The announcement of the Partition Plan
The first session of the Constituent Assembly

What was the so-called Pig War between the United States and Britain over?
The Pig War of 1859 was a border dispute over San Juan Island; it began after an American farmer shot a British-owned pig. The only casualty was the pig.
The dispute was settled by arbitration in 1872 in favour of the United States.
According to the Hadith, what will a person be asked about first on the Day of Judgement regarding the rights of Allah?
The Prophet (PBUH) said that the first thing a servant will be called to account for on the Day of Judgement is prayer (Salah).
Regarding rights between people, the first matter judged will be bloodshed.
When an ant stings, which acid is injected into the body?
Ant venom contains formic acid, which causes the burning pain of the sting.
Formic acid gets its name from the Latin word formica meaning ant.
When did the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic begin?
The first cases were reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.

In which year did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh?
East Pakistan broke away after the 1971 war, and the Dhaka surrender took place on 16 December 1971.

In which year of the Hijri calendar did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Umrat-ul-Qaza?

Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam in the 6th year of prophethood, after the Prophet's prayer that Allah strengthen Islam through one of the two Umars.

Hinda bint Utbah, who had opposed Islam at Uhud, accepted Islam when Makkah was conquered in 8 AH.

When did India first present the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
India took the Kashmir dispute to the UN Security Council on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.

What was the legislature setup under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?

In which year did the First World War end?

In which year did the Second World War end?
