The United Nations was founded in the same year, 1945.
In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India?
The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and announced its plan in May 1946. It proposed a loose federation, which the Congress and the Muslim League accepted only briefly.
The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.
In which year was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in India?
Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat leaders, against British rule. Indians boycotted British courts, schools and goods.
Gandhi suspended the movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
Around which year did the Ottoman Sultanate begin under Osman I?
Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299. It lasted until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.
The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 under Sultan Muhammad II (Mehmed the Conqueror).
On which date did the United Nations officially come into existence?
The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after ratification by China, France, the USSR, the UK, the USA and most other signatories. This date is celebrated as United Nations Day.
The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
On which date is Kashmir Day (Kashmir Solidarity Day) observed in Pakistan?
Pakistan observes Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February every year to express support for the people of Indian-held Kashmir.
Kashmiris also observe 27 October as Black Day, the day Indian troops landed in Srinagar in 1947.
In which year did the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College, Aligarh, begin as a college?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded a school in 1875, which was raised to college level as the MAO College in 1877. Lord Lytton laid its foundation stone in 1877.
The MAO College became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk fought?
The Ghazwa of Tabuk took place in 9 AH (630 CE) against the Byzantine threat on the northern frontier. The Prophet (PBUH) led about 30,000 Muslims, but no fighting occurred.
Tabuk is also called Ghazwa-e-Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship, because of the heat and shortage of supplies.
In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory (according to the most commonly taught view)?
Most Pakistani textbooks teach that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH. The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj that year.
Sources differ, as some scholars give 6 AH or 10 AH; the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 AH.
In which year was the state of Israel declared?
Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate over Palestine ended. The first Arab-Israeli war followed immediately.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Palestine partition plan in November 1947.
In which year was the National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) established?
The National Bank of Pakistan was established in November 1949 to help finance the agricultural sector, notably the jute and cotton crops. It later acted as an agent of the State Bank.
The State Bank of Pakistan began working earlier, on 1 July 1948.
In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver his Last (Farewell) Sermon?
The Prophet (PBUH) delivered the Last Sermon during the Farewell Hajj on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (632 CE), at Arafat. He passed away in 11 AH.
The sermon was delivered at Mount Arafat in the valley of Uranah.
In which year did Choudhary Rahmat Ali write the pamphlet 'Now or Never'?
Choudhary Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues issued the pamphlet 'Now or Never' in January 1933. It first proposed the name Pakistan for a Muslim homeland.
Rahmat Ali is known as the person who coined the name Pakistan.
In which year was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) established by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
The RCD was formally established in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic cooperation. It replaced the earlier CENTO-linked arrangements in the economic field.
The RCD was succeeded by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
In which year was the Second Battle of Panipat fought between Akbar's army and Hemu?
The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556, when Akbar's general Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. It secured the Mughal throne for Akbar.
The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was won by Babur against Ibrahim Lodhi.
On what date did the State Bank of Pakistan begin operations?
The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah on 1 July 1948. It took over the work of the Reserve Bank of India for Pakistan.
Its first governor was Zahid Hussain.
On what date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973, and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. It was authenticated by President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was the Prime Minister when the Constitution was enacted.
In which year was the United Nations Organization (UNO) formed?
The United Nations officially came into existence on 24 October 1945 after the UN Charter was ratified.
Its predecessor, the League of Nations, was formed in 1919.
In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT arrangement.
The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
In which province of Pakistan are the Chagai Hills located?
The Chagai Hills lie in Chagai district in the northwest of Balochistan, near the Afghan and Iranian borders.
Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests of May 1998 in the Chagai Hills.
At which place did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address of 1930 in which he presented the idea of a separate Muslim state?
Iqbal delivered the Presidential Address at the annual session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad in December 1930.
The Lahore Resolution was passed ten years later, in March 1940.
Which country is regarded as the place of origin of the game of chess?
Chess developed from the ancient Indian game Chaturanga in about the 6th century AD, and then spread to Persia and the world.
The word checkmate comes from the Persian shah mat.
In which region does the Yellow River (Huang He) of China originate?
The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai province on the Tibetan Plateau and flows east to the Bohai Sea.
It is the second longest river in China after the Yangtze.
In which country is Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located?
Angel Falls (Salto Angel) is in Canaima National Park in Bolivar state, Venezuela.
Where is Jabal-e-Noor (the mountain containing the Cave of Hira) located?
Jabal al-Noor is a mountain near Makkah in Saudi Arabia and holds the Cave of Hira where the first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH).
The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, was received in this cave.
In which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is Khanpur Dam located?
Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It supplies water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Lake Superior is the northernmost of the Great Lakes and lies between the USA and Canada in North America.
It is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.
Where is the MAO College (founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) located?
The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
It later became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
In which city is the Margalla Hills National Park located?
The Margalla Hills form the northern backdrop of Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
Faisal Mosque lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills.
In which district of Sindh are the ruins of Mohenjo-daro located?
Mohenjo-daro lies near Dokri in Larkana district, Sindh, on the right bank of the Indus.
It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
Which Indian Ocean water body is the Bay of Bengal part of?
The Bay of Bengal is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.
It is the largest bay in the world.
Between which two countries does the Bay of Bothnia lie?
The Gulf or Bay of Bothnia is the northern arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland.
It is the northernmost part of the Baltic Sea.
Between which countries does the Gulf (Bay) of Riga lie?
The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea bordered by Latvia and Estonia.
Its main port is Riga, the capital of Latvia.
In which country is Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
Shark Bay is on the coast of Western Australia.
It was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1991.
In which region was the ancient Gandhara civilization centred?
Gandhara flourished in the Peshawar valley and Potohar region of northwest Pakistan, with Taxila and Peshawar as major centres.
Gandhara art is famous for Greco-Buddhist sculpture.
Where is the headquarters of SAARC located?
The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987.
SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka.
Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
The UN headquarters is on the east side of Manhattan in New York City, USA.
The UN also has major offices at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.
Where is the headquarters of the World Bank located?
The World Bank has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., USA. It was set up in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is also headquartered in Washington, D.C.
Where is the headquarters of OPEC located?
OPEC moved from Geneva to Vienna, Austria in 1965 and has been headquartered there since.
OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960.
In which region of Pakistan does the River Soan flow?
The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar Plateau near Rawalpindi and Islamabad before joining the Indus.
The Soan valley is known for Stone Age sites.
In which city or area is Simly Dam located?
Simly Dam is on the Soan River in the Islamabad Capital Territory, about 30 km from the city.
It is a major source of drinking water for Islamabad.
Where is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) located?
Data Ganj Bakhsh, the author of Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, is buried in Lahore near Bhati Gate. His shrine is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
His death anniversary (Urs) is held every year at the shrine in Lahore.
Where is the tomb of the Punjabi poet Waris Shah located?
Waris Shah, author of the epic Heer Ranjha, is buried at Jandiala Sher Khan in Sheikhupura district, where he died in 1798.
Waris Shah was born in Jandiala Sher Khan and wrote Heer in 1766.
Where is the Zhob River situated?
The Zhob River rises in Balochistan and flows through the Zhob district, joining the Gomal River.
The Gomal River later flows into the Indus River system through Dera Ismail Khan.
Where is the world's largest active volcano, Mauna Loa, located?
Mauna Loa is on the Big Island of Hawaii and is regarded as the largest active volcano on Earth by volume. It erupted in November 2022 for the first time since 1984.
Mount Etna in Italy is Europe's most active volcano.
The Yangtze and the Yellow River are the two longest rivers of which country?
Both the Yangtze and the Yellow River (Huang He) flow through China and empty into the sea on its east coast. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
The Yellow River is called the cradle of Chinese civilization.
Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated in December 2007?
Benazir Bhutto was killed on 27 December 2007 after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. She was attacked as she left the venue.
She had been Prime Minister of Pakistan twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.
In which city was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan, assassinated in 1951?
Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.
Which agreement was signed between Pakistan and India in January 1966 after the 1965 war?
The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri. It ended the 1965 war and restored the earlier positions.
The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin mediated the talks.
In which city was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
The Tashkent Declaration was signed in Tashkent, then in the Soviet Union and now the capital of Uzbekistan.
Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent the day after the signing.
Which agreement was signed between Pakistan and India after the 1971 war?
The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi. It set the Line of Control in Kashmir.
The Lahore Declaration followed much later, in 1999.
Where was the atomic test of Pakistan conducted on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan on 28 May 1998.
Where was the Battle of Khaibar fought?
Near Khaibar oasis north of Madinah, Arabia
The Battle of Khaibar was fought in 628-629 AD (7 AH) against the Jewish fortresses at the Khaibar oasis in Arabia. Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus.
The Khyber Pass in Pakistan is a different place with a similar name.
Where was the first OIC summit held in 1969?
The first Islamic Summit was held in Rabat, Morocco in September 1969 after the arson at Al-Aqsa Mosque.
The second Islamic Summit was held in Lahore in 1974.
Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah.
The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old at that time.
Which acid is found in milk?
Sour milk contains lactic acid, formed when bacteria ferment lactose. Fresh milk is only slightly acidic.
Citric acid is found in lemons and oranges.
Which military alliance was formed in 1955 by the Soviet bloc in response to NATO?
The Warsaw Pact was signed in 1955 by the USSR and its eastern European allies as a counter to NATO.
The Warsaw Pact was dissolved in 1991.
Which angel will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement?
Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Sur to end the world and again to raise the dead.
Hazrat Azrail (AS) is the angel of death.
Which angels write down the good and bad deeds of every human being?
Kiraman Katibin are the two noble recording angels on a person's shoulders who write the deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.
Munkar and Nakir are the angels who question a person in the grave.
Which batsman scored 400 not out in a Test innings?
Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004. It is the highest individual score in Test cricket.
Matthew Hayden's 380 was the previous record before Lara's 400.
Which body regulates electronic media in Pakistan?
The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) regulates private television and radio channels.
Which child was the first to embrace Islam?
Hazrat Ali (RA), a boy of about ten, was the first child to accept Islam. Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man.
Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is often named as the first freed slave to accept Islam.
Which city has the highest population in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
Peshawar is the capital and the most populous city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Mardan is generally the second largest city of the province.
Which city has the highest population in Punjab?
Lahore is the capital and the most populous city of Punjab, and the second largest in Pakistan.
Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.
Which city is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya)?
Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines of Sufi saints, such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.
Multan is also known as the City of Mangoes.
Which commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary line between Pakistan and India in 1947?
The Boundary Commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe demarcated the Punjab and Bengal borders, and the line is called the Radcliffe Line. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.
The Radcliffe Award was announced after independence, on 17 August 1947.
Which of the following Sahabah was NOT among the Ashra Mubashira (the ten companions given the glad tidings of Paradise)?
Talha, Zubair and Abdur Rahman bin Auf are all in the list of ten promised Paradise in one hadith. Abu Hurairah, a great narrator of hadith, is not in that list.
The ten are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (RA).
Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) addressed King Najashi of Abyssinia on behalf of the Muslim migrants?
Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib was the spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He recited verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi.
Najashi later accepted Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.
Which companion served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years in Madina?
Hazrat Anas bin Malik was given to the Prophet as a boy servant and served him for about ten years in Madina.
He narrated more than two thousand hadith.
Which corridor separates Pakistan from Tajikistan and the Central Asian states?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan. It is about 350 km long and 13 to 65 km wide.
The Wakhan Corridor also touches China at its eastern end.
In which country is the Wakhan Corridor situated?
The Wakhan Corridor is a strip of land in the north-east of Afghanistan in Badakhshan province.
It was created as a buffer between the British and Russian empires in the 19th century.
Which of the following are the Scandinavian countries?
The Scandinavian countries are Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
Finland and Iceland are usually counted with them as Nordic countries.
Which two countries share the border that mostly follows the 49th parallel north?
Much of the border between the contiguous United States and Canada runs along the 49th parallel north.
The 49th parallel was fixed by the Treaty of 1818 and the Oregon Treaty of 1846.
Which country is shaped like a long boot on the map?
Italy is a peninsula that looks like a long boot kicking the island of Sicily.
Rome, the capital of Italy, was the centre of the ancient Roman Empire.
The 1996 Cricket World Cup was co-hosted by Pakistan along with which two countries?
The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka won the title by beating Australia in the final at Lahore.
The 1996 final was played at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore.
Which country was the first to recognise Pakistan after its creation in 1947, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Most Pakistani textbooks state that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan. Iran also sent the first ambassador.
Sources differ, as some also credit Turkey, and Afghanistan opposed Pakistan's UN membership.
Which country supplied S-400 air defence missile systems to India?
India signed a deal in 2018 with Russia for S-400 Triumf air defence systems. Deliveries began in 2021.
The S-400 is a Russian long range surface to air missile system.
Which country is the world's largest producer of cotton?
China is the leading producer of cotton, with most of its crop grown in Xinjiang. India is second.
Pakistan is usually among the top five cotton producers.
Which country hosted the third modern Olympic Games in 1904?
The third modern Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri, USA in 1904. The first was in Athens in 1896 and the second in Paris in 1900.
The 1904 Games were the first Olympics held outside Europe.
Which of the following was NOT a member of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) formed in 1964?
The RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey. Afghanistan was never a member.
RCD was replaced by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.
China and the United States follow closely as third and fourth.
Which country is the world's largest exporter of arms?
According to SIPRI, the United States is the largest arms exporter and supplies around 40 percent of global arms exports.
France has recently overtaken Russia as the second largest arms exporter.
Which country is known as the Land of the Long White Cloud?
The Maori name Aotearoa is translated as Land of the Long White Cloud and refers to New Zealand.
Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.
Which country is the world's largest producer of chromite (chromium ore)?
According to USGS data, South Africa is by far the largest chromite producer, with about 22.9 million tonnes in 2024. Kazakhstan is second.
South Africa also holds the largest chromite reserves in the world.
Which two countries jointly developed the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
The JF-17 Thunder was jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (PAC) Kamra and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
Myanmar was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17.
Which cricket league is played in Pakistan?
The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the professional Twenty20 league of Pakistan. It started in 2016.
Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and 2023.
Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record for the fastest century in One Day Internationals?
Afridi scored a century off 37 balls in 1996. Corey Anderson of New Zealand reached a hundred in 36 balls against West Indies in January 2014 and broke it.
AB de Villiers later took the record with a 31-ball century against West Indies in 2015.
Which international day does the United Nations observe on 24 June?
International Day of Women in Diplomacy
The UN General Assembly declared 24 June as the International Day of Women in Diplomacy in 2022. It promotes the participation of women in diplomacy.
World Refugee Day is on 20 June and International Widows Day is on 23 June.
Which day is celebrated in Pakistan in memory of the nuclear tests of 1998?
Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998. The day is observed every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.
The tests were carried out in response to the Indian nuclear tests of May 1998.
Which famous musician was born in Salzburg, Austria?
Mozart was born in Salzburg on 27 January 1756. Beethoven was born in Bonn, Bach in Eisenach and Schubert in Vienna.
Mozart composed more than 600 works before his death in Vienna in 1791.
Which game is played on a court enclosed by four walls?
Squash is played in a closed court with four walls, and the ball may be hit off any wall except for out-of-play lines.
Squash was invented in England at Harrow School in the 19th century and Pakistan has been a champion nation in it.
Which Ghazwa (battle) is called Yaum ul Furqan, the day of distinction between right and wrong?
The Quran calls the day of the Battle of Badr (2 AH) Yaum ul Furqan because truth was clearly separated from falsehood.
About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1000 Quraish at Badr.
Which was the last Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) personally took part?
The Ghazwa of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last military expedition led personally by the Prophet (PBUH).
Tabuk is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the expedition of hardship.
Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan?
OGRA was established in 2002 to regulate the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector. NDMA handles disasters, WAPDA water and power, PEMRA electronic media.
OGRA also recommends the prices of petroleum products and natural gas.
Which is the coldest desert in the world?
The Antarctic Desert is the coldest and largest desert on Earth, with extremely low rainfall and temperatures far below freezing.
The Gobi is the best known cold desert of Asia, but it is much warmer than Antarctica.
The verb profit ends in a single t, and the stress is on the first syllable, so the consonant is not doubled: profited.
The same rule gives benefited and budgeted.
Which is the deepest ocean in the world?
The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point.
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 11,000 metres deep.
Which was the first qiblah of the Muslims?
Bait ul Muqaddas (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem
Muslims prayed towards Bait ul Muqaddas for about 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah. The qiblah was then changed to the Kaaba.
The change took place in 2 AH in the Masjid Qiblatain in Madinah.
Which is the highest capital city of the world?
La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, stands at about 3,640 metres above sea level, higher than any other capital.
Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, and Quito is the highest official capital.
Which is the highest highway of Pakistan?
The Karakoram Highway reaches about 4,693 metres at the Khunjerab Pass on the China border, the highest paved international road.
It links Hasan Abdal in Pakistan with Kashgar in China.
Which is the highest peak of Pakistan?
K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen) is 8,611 metres high, the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world.
Nanga Parbat at 8,126 metres is the second highest peak in Pakistan.
Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan and the world?
The Shandur polo ground at Shandur Pass is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world.
A famous polo festival between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan is held at Shandur every year.
Which mountain is known as the Killer Mountain?
Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it in early attempts.
Nanga Parbat means Naked Mountain and is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
Which is the largest airport in the world by area?
King Fahd International Airport (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
King Fahd International Airport near Dammam covers about 776 to 780 square kilometres, far more than any other airport.
Denver International Airport is second largest at about 136 square kilometres.
Which is the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by population?
Peshawar, the provincial capital, has the largest population in the province according to the 2023 census.
Mardan is generally ranked as the second largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Which is the largest country of Asia by population?
India overtook China in 2023 and is now the most populous country in both Asia and the world, with about 1.45 billion people.
Earlier, China was the most populous country, which was the answer in 2021-22.
Which country is called the largest democracy in the world?
India has the largest electorate and the largest population of any democracy. It is called the world's largest democracy.
India overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023.
Which is the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan?
Pashtuns form the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, roughly 40 percent of the population.
Tajiks are the second largest ethnic group of Afghanistan.
Which is the largest gulf in the world by area?
The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.55 million square kilometres, the largest gulf in the world.
The Persian Gulf is far smaller, at about 251,000 square kilometres.
Which is the largest lake of East Africa?
Lake Victoria covers about 68,800 square kilometres and is the largest lake in Africa by area.
Lake Victoria is the source of the White Nile.
Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
Kazakhstan has an area of about 2.72 million square kilometres and no coastline on an ocean. It is the largest landlocked country.
Mongolia is the second largest landlocked country.
Which is the largest man-made lake (reservoir) of Pakistan?
Tarbela Reservoir on the Indus has the largest surface area of any reservoir in Pakistan, about 250 square kilometres.
Tarbela Dam is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
Which is the largest non-polar desert in the world?
The Sahara covers about 9.2 million square kilometres, the largest hot (non-polar) desert.
Antarctica is the largest desert overall, followed by the Arctic and then the Sahara.
Which is the largest salt mine of Pakistan?
The Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district is the largest salt mine in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
Khewra salt is mostly rock salt, known as Himalayan pink salt.
Which is the longest river in the world according to most textbooks?
Most textbooks give the Nile as the longest river, at about 6,650 kilometres.
Some sources measure the Amazon as longer, so sources differ.
Which is the most populous city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
Peshawar is the provincial capital and the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities of South Asia.
Which is the most populous city of Pakistan?
Karachi is Pakistan's largest city, with about 20 million people in the 2023 census.
Karachi is the capital of Sindh and was Pakistan's first capital.
Which is the most populous province of Pakistan?
Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population, over 127 million in the 2023 census.
Balochistan is the largest province by area but has the smallest population.
Which is the national news agency of Pakistan?
Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) is the state-run national news agency of Pakistan.
APP was nationalised in 1961 and has its headquarters in Islamabad.
Which is the wettest place in the world (the one most commonly named in textbooks)?
Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India, receives the highest average annual rainfall of any inhabited place, over 11,000 mm.
Nearby Cherrapunji was once named the wettest place, so sources differ.
In the Islamic calendar, which is the year called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
In the 10th year of Prophethood, both Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.
Which lines are called parallel lines?
Lines that intersect at a right angle
Lines in the same plane that never meet
Lines that meet at one point
Parallel lines lie in the same plane and stay the same distance apart, so they never meet however far they are extended.
A line that cuts two parallel lines is called a transversal.
Which mountain (peak) lies on the border between China and Pakistan?
K2 in the Karakoram lies on the China-Pakistan border, between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
At 8,611 m, K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.
Which mountain range lies between France and Italy?
The Alps, including Mont Blanc, mark part of the border between France and Italy.
Mont Blanc, at about 4,800 m, is the highest peak in the Alps.
Which mountain range separates Spain and France?
The Pyrenees run between France and Spain.
Andorra lies within the Pyrenees between France and Spain.
Which obligatory act is mentioned in the Quran most often together with Zakat?
The Quran repeatedly pairs the command to establish Salah with the command to pay Zakat.
The phrase 'Aqeemus-Salah wa Atuz-Zakah' occurs many times in the Quran.
Which ocean lies along the coast of Pakistan?
Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km is on the Arabian Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean.
Karachi, Gwadar and Port Qasim are Pakistan's main ports.
Which of the following does not mean big: huge, massive, scrap?
Huge and massive both mean very large, while scrap means a small piece or leftover.
Scrap can also mean to discard something as useless.
Which ancient civilization flourished in Taxila?
Taxila was a major city of the Gandhara civilization and a famed centre of learning.
Taxila was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
Which Pakistani army operation was launched nationwide in February 2017?
Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was announced on 22 February 2017 after a wave of terror attacks across Pakistan.
Zarb-e-Azb began in June 2014 and Rah-e-Rast in 2009.
Which principal organ of the United Nations is no longer active (suspended operations)?
The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after Palau, the last trust territory, became independent.
The other five principal organs are still functioning.
Which organization oversees international civil aviation?
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a UN agency, sets global standards for civil aviation.
ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
Which Pakistani batter holds the highest individual score in Test cricket for Pakistan?
Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958, still Pakistan's highest Test score.
Younis Khan's 313 against Sri Lanka in 2009 is the second highest by a Pakistani.
Which is the world's largest silver producing country?
Mexico leads the world in mined silver, at about 173 million ounces in 2025, ahead of Peru and China.
Mexico has been the top silver producer for many years.
Which Pakistani scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1979?
Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the unified electroweak theory.
Abdus Salam is the only Pakistani Nobel laureate in Physics; Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
Which political party did Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto found?
Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto founded the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in Lahore.
The PPP was founded in November 1967 on the slogan of roti, kapra aur makan.
Which pillar of Islam is mentioned in the Quran many times together with zakat?
The Quran repeatedly joins the command 'establish prayer and give zakat'.
Salah and zakat are paired in dozens of verses of the Quran.
Which planet is named after the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Zeus?
Jupiter is the Roman name of the king of the gods, whom the Greeks called Zeus.
Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system.
Which planet comes closest to the Earth?
Venus approaches Earth to about 38 million km, closer than any other planet.
Some recent calculations show Mercury is nearest on average over time, but textbooks give Venus.
Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
Hazrat Musa (AS) is named about 136 times in the Quran, more than any other prophet.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is the next most frequently mentioned prophet.
Which prophet built the ark (boat) at the command of Allah before the great flood?
Allah commanded Hazrat Nuh (AS) to build the ark to save the believers from the flood.
Surah Nuh of the Quran is named after this prophet.
Which prophet was given a great kingdom, including rule over the jinn and the winds?
Allah gave Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) a unique kingdom, with jinn, birds and winds under his command.
Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawud (AS), who was also a prophet and king.
Which Sahabi is known by the title Jame ul Quran (compiler of the Quran)?
Hazrat Uthman (RA) had the Quran copied into one standard text and sent copies to the major cities.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first gathered the Quran into one volume after the Battle of Yamama.
Which Sahabi did the Prophet (PBUH) call the door of knowledge?
A hadith reports the Prophet (PBUH) saying: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.
Which Sahabi was known as the keeper of the secrets (Sahib-ul-Sirr) of the Prophet (PBUH)?
The Prophet (PBUH) confided to Hudhayfah bin al-Yaman (RA) the names of the hypocrites, so he was called Sahib-ul-Sirr.
Hazrat Umar (RA) used to ask Hudhayfah whether his own name was among the hypocrites.
Which preposition completes the sentence: 'He reminded me ___ my History teacher'?
The verb 'remind' takes 'of' when something resembles or recalls another person or thing.
'Remind someone about' is used for a task or duty, for example remind me about the meeting.
Which preposition is used with 'laugh' when making fun of someone: 'laughed ___ someone'?
To laugh at someone means to mock them; 'laugh at' is the correct phrasal form.
'Laugh with someone' means to share the joke in a friendly way.
Which province of Pakistan has the largest number of National Assembly seats?
Punjab has 141 of the 266 general seats of the National Assembly, far more than any other province.
The National Assembly has 336 seats in total, including 60 for women and 10 for non-Muslims.
Which province of Pakistan has the largest provincial assembly?
The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab has 371 seats, more than the other three assemblies.
Sindh has 168 seats, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 145 and Balochistan 65.
Which surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant?
Surah Al-Naml (the Ant), the 27th surah, takes its name from the story of the ant that warned its colony about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and his army.
Al-Nahl is the surah named after the bee and Al-Ankabut the one named after the spider.
Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect?
The Panama Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama and joins the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean. This saves ships the long voyage around South America.
The Panama Canal was opened in 1914.
Which two surahs of the Holy Quran are together called Muawwazatain?
Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah Al-Nas (114) both begin with a request to seek refuge (ta'awwuz) with Allah. That is why the pair is called Muawwazatain.
These are the last two surahs of the Quran and are commonly recited for protection.
Which was the first Muslim country to become a nuclear power?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998 and became the first Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-armed country in the world, after India's tests earlier in May 1998.
Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) and was married to the Prophet (PBUH). Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).
Hazrat Aisha (RA) is one of the most important narrators of hadith.
Which defensive technique was used by the Muslims in the Battle of Khandaq (Trench) in 5 AH?
Building a wall of stones around Makkah
Fighting from the hills of Uhud
A night surprise attack on the enemy camp
On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA), the Muslims dug a long trench across the open side of Madinah. The Quraish and their allies could not cross it and had to retreat.
The battle is also called the Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates).
Who appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor and teacher of Yemen?
Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen around 10 AH as governor, judge and teacher of the Quran and Islamic law.
Before sending him, the Prophet (PBUH) asked how he would judge, and he replied: by the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning (ijtihad).
Who are called Ahl ul Bait?
All the companions of the Prophet (PBUH)
The family members of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
Ahl ul Bait means the people of the house, that is the family of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), including his wives, daughter Fatimah (RA), Hazrat Ali (RA) and their children.
The Quran addresses the Ahl ul Bait in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 33.
Which of the following was a daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Aisha, Hafsa and Khadija (RA) were his wives.
All the daughters were born to Hazrat Khadija (RA).
Who is called the Hawari (special helper) of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
On the day of Khandaq the Prophet (PBUH) said that every prophet has a Hawari and his Hawari is Zubair (RA), as recorded in Sahih Bukhari.
The word Hawari is also used in the Quran for the disciples of Prophet Isa (AS).
Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record of the fastest century in ODIs (37 balls, 1996)?
New Zealand's Corey Anderson scored a century off 36 balls against the West Indies in January 2014 and broke Afridi's 17-year-old record.
AB de Villiers later broke Anderson's record with a 31-ball century against the West Indies in January 2015, and it still stands.
Who broke Shahid Afridi's record for the most sixes in One Day Internationals?
Rohit Sharma hit his 352nd ODI six on 30 November 2025 against South Africa at Ranchi, passing Afridi's 351.
Chris Gayle, with 331 sixes, is third on the all-time ODI list.
Masjid-e-Zarrar was built by hypocrites near Quba as a base for harming Muslims and dividing them, and the Prophet (PBUH) ordered it to be demolished.
Its story is mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah, verse 107.
Who compiled the hadith collection Sahih Muslim?
Sahih Muslim was compiled by Imam Muslim bin al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi (died 261 AH).
Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are known as the Sahihain.
Who conducts and governs the modern Olympic Games?
The International Olympic Committee, founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin, organises the modern Olympic Games.
The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Who elects the members of the Senate of Pakistan from the provinces?
The members of the Provincial Assemblies
Senators from each province are elected indirectly by the members of that provincial Assembly through the single transferable vote system.
The Senate is a permanent house with half of its members retiring every three years.
Who first raised the Kashmir issue in the United Nations Security Council, and when?
India lodged a complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, and the Security Council took up the matter.
Pakistan replied with its own complaint on 15 January 1948.
Who founded the technology company Microsoft?
Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft on 4 April 1975.
Microsoft began in Albuquerque, New Mexico, before moving to Washington State.
Who gave the first Azan in Islam?
Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA) was appointed by the Prophet (PBUH) as the first muezzin and called the first Azan in Madinah.
Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the Azan in a dream, and the Prophet (PBUH) taught them to Bilal (RA).
Who introduced the fictional spy character James Bond?
Ian Fleming created James Bond in the novel Casino Royale, published in 1953.
Fleming had worked in British naval intelligence during the Second World War.
Who is known as the father of the hydrogen bomb?
Edward Teller, working with Stanislaw Ulam, is credited with the design of the hydrogen bomb, first tested in 1952.
Robert Oppenheimer is known as the father of the atomic bomb; sources sometimes also credit Ulam alongside Teller.
The uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who opposed him
The leader of the Banu Quraiza
Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza bin Abdul Muttalib) was an uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who strongly opposed Islam.
Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) of the Quran was revealed about him.
Who was Baba Farid (Hazrat Fariduddin Ganj Shakar)?
A Sufi saint of the Chishti order
A poet of the Sikh court
Baba Farid (1179-1266) was a famous Punjabi Sufi saint and poet of the Chishti order, and a disciple of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
His shrine is in Pakpattan, and his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Which Caliph is known as Jami-ul-Quran?
Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called Jami-ul-Quran because he had the Quran compiled in one standard text and sent copies to the major cities.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first collected the Quran in written form after the Battle of Yamama.
Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in One Day Internationals?
Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 11,701 runs in ODIs, the most for Pakistan.
Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him on the list.
Which angel is responsible for rain and sustenance according to Islamic belief?
Hazrat Mikaeel (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
Hazrat Israfeel (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgement.
Who wrote Humayun Nama, an account of the reign of Emperor Humayun?
Gulbadan Begum, a daughter of Babur and aunt of Akbar, wrote Humayun Nama.
Akbar had asked her to record her memories for Abul Fazl's Akbarnama.
Who was the half-brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was a son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) from Hazrat Sarah, while Hazrat Ismail (AS) was his son from Hazrat Hajra, so they were half-brothers.
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
Mir Sarfraz Bugti took office as Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and was still serving in mid-2026.
His predecessors included Abdul Quddus Bizenjo (2021-2023) and Jam Kamal Khan (2018-2021).
Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy?
Admiral Naveed Ashraf took over as Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023 and is the serving chief in 2026.
His predecessors were Admiral Muhammad Zakaullah and, before him, Admiral Muhammad Amjad Khan Niazi.
Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
Mir Sarfraz Bugti of the Pakistan Peoples Party was elected Chief Minister of Balochistan unopposed in March 2024 and still holds the office.
Jam Kamal Khan, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Chief Minister from 2018 to 2021.
Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
Sardar Ayaz Sadiq of the PML-N was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024 and is the current Speaker.
Asad Qaiser, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Speaker from 2018 to 2022.
Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan?
Khawaja Muhammad Asif of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Defence in the current government.
Pervez Khattak, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Defence Minister from 2018 to 2022.
Who is the Federal Minister for Railways of Pakistan?
Muhammad Hanif Abbasi of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Railways in the current government.
Khawaja Saad Rafique held the same ministry in the 2022-23 coalition government.
Who is the Federal Minister for Interior of Pakistan?
Mohsin Naqvi is the Federal Interior Minister in the current government.
He is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and president of the Asian Cricket Council.
Who is the Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab?
Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan of the PML-N has been Speaker of the Punjab Assembly since February 2024.
He is a lawyer from Kasur and was earlier a Special Assistant to the Chief Minister.
Who is the President of France?
Emmanuel Macron was first elected President of France in 2017 and re-elected in 2022; he is still in office.
The French President is elected for a five-year term.
Who is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
Andy Burnham became UK Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer stepped down as Labour leader.
Boris Johnson, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Prime Minister from 2019 to 2022.
Who is the son of Hazrat Hajira (A.S)?
Hazrat Hajira was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S).
The well of Zamzam sprang up near the infant Ismail (A.S) in Makkah.
Who is the son of Hazrat Maryam (A.S)?
Hazrat Maryam (A.S) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (A.S), born without a father by Allah's command.
Surah Maryam in the Holy Quran is named after her.
Who is known as the Traveler of Islam?
Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan scholar, traveled across much of the Muslim world and beyond for about 30 years and is called the Traveler of Islam.
His travel account is known as the Rihla.
Who is the writer of the book The Spirit of Islam?
The Spirit of Islam (1891) was written by Syed Ameer Ali.
Ameer Ali also wrote A Short History of the Saracens.
Who is the writer of the book Becoming?
Becoming (2018) is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
It became one of the best-selling memoirs of all time.
Who is the compiler of Tirmizi Sharif (Jami at-Tirmidhi)?
Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Isa at-Tirmidhi.
It is one of the six major Hadith collections known as the Sihah Sitta.
Who is the Pakistani who most recently won a Nobel Prize?
Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, which makes her the latest Pakistani Nobel laureate.
Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate, winning the Physics prize in 1979.
Who is the youngest Nobel Prize winner in history?
Malala Yousafzai was 17 years old when she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, the youngest laureate ever.
Lawrence Bragg, aged 25, was the youngest laureate in a science field (Physics, 1915).
Who is known as Zunoorain (the possessor of two lights)?
Hazrat Usman (R.A) is called Zunoorain because he married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W), Hazrat Ruqayyah and then Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A).
He was the third Caliph of Islam.
Who served the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) for ten years in Madinah?
Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet (S.A.W) as a boy by his mother and served him for about ten years.
Which Companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) is known as Sahib-e-Sirr (keeper of the secrets) of the Prophet?
Hazrat Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman (R.A) was entrusted with the Prophet's secrets, including the names of the hypocrites.
Hazrat Umar (R.A) used to ask him whether his own name was among the hypocrites.
Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from Harvard University with his college roommates.
The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.
Who appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (R.A) as governor of Yemen?
The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (R.A) to Yemen as governor and judge.
The Prophet asked him how he would judge, and he replied by the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning (ijtihad).
Who is the father of Hazrat Usman (R.A)?
Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the son of Affan bin Abi al-As of the Banu Umayya clan of Quraysh.
Abu Quhafa was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Khattab the father of Hazrat Umar (R.A).
Who is called the father of modern chemistry?
Antoine Lavoisier is commonly called the father of modern chemistry for his work on oxygen and the law of conservation of mass.
Some sources give this title to Robert Boyle, so sources differ.
Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
Florence Nightingale established modern nursing practice and training after her work in the Crimean War.
She founded the Nightingale School of Nursing in London in 1860, and International Nurses Day is on her birthday, 12 May.
Who mediated between Pakistan and India in the Tashkent Agreement of January 1966?
The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent. The agreement ended the 1965 war.
Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it, and Shastri died in Tashkent the next day.
Which country opposed Pakistan's admission to the United Nations in 1947?
Afghanistan was the only country that voted against Pakistan's membership of the UN in September 1947. It later withdrew its objection.
Pakistan became the 56th member of the United Nations on 30 September 1947.
Who first proposed the name Pakistan?
Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
Allama Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address proposed a separate Muslim state but did not use the name Pakistan.
Who recited Surah Maryam before the king Najashi of Abyssinia?
Hazrat Jaffar bin Abi Talib spoke for the Muslim migrants and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved Najashi and the bishops.
Hazrat Jaffar was later martyred at the Battle of Mutah and is known as Tayyar.
Who refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature?
The French writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, saying he refused official honours.
Boris Pasternak was forced by Soviet authorities to decline his 1958 Nobel Prize.
Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical form of the Quran?
When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha replied that his character was the Quran.
This report is found in Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad.
Who scored 400 not out in a Test innings, the highest individual Test score?
Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004.
Matthew Hayden's 380 was the record before Lara, and Lara's 400 not out still stands in 2026.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, by whom are the senators of the provinces elected?
The members of the provincial assembly
Senators for each province are elected by the members of that provincial assembly by the single transferable vote.
The Senate has a Chairman who acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
Who sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal as governor and teacher of Yemen around 10 AH.
The Prophet asked him how he would judge, and he replied by the Quran, then Sunnah, then his own reasoning.
Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of Pakistan?
President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Simla Agreement with the Indian Prime Minister in July 1972.
The agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.
Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of India?
Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement for India opposite Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
The Line of Control in Kashmir was established under this agreement.
Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in India in 1920?
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat Movement.
It was called off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
Who acts as the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to perform the functions of office?
The Speaker of the National Assembly
Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President. If there is no Chairman, the Speaker of the National Assembly does so.
Muhammad Mian Soomro and Wasim Sajjad are among Senate Chairmen who have acted as President.
Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
Babur defeated the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat on 21 April 1526, which began Mughal rule in India.
Babur used artillery and field tactics learned from the Ottomans.
Who was the opponent of Field Marshal Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election of Pakistan?
Miss Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, contested as the joint candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties in January 1965. Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats electoral college.
She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
Who were the Banu Nadir (Banu Nuzair) in the history of Madina?
A branch of the Aws tribe
Banu Nadir was a Jewish tribe living near Madina. They were exiled in 4 AH after plotting against the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
The other Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qainuqa and Banu Quraiza.
Who became the Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan after Yahya Khan in December 1971?
After the fall of Dhaka, Yahya Khan handed power to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became President and the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Martial law was lifted when the 1973 Constitution came into force.
Who was the husband of Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
Hazrat Ayesha, daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr, was married to the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
She is known as Umm ul Momineen and narrated over two thousand hadith.
Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister. After his assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second.
Nazimuddin had been Governor-General before becoming Prime Minister.
Who was the second President of Pakistan?
Iskander Mirza was the first President under the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan removed him in 1958 and became the second.
Counts differ if the Governor-General office is included, but textbooks list Ayub Khan second.
Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war with India?
General Muhammad Musa Khan was Commander-in-Chief from 1958 to 1966 and led the army in the 1965 war.
Yahya Khan succeeded him as Commander-in-Chief in 1966.
Who was the closest friend of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) was the Prophet's closest friend and the first man outside his family circle to accept Islam. He is called Siddique and Yar-e-Ghar (companion of the cave).
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first caliph of Islam and ruled from 11 AH to 13 AH.
Who accompanied the Holy Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrat from Makkah to Madina?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the Prophet's companion on the Hijrat and shared the cave of Thaur with him. Hazrat Ali (RA) stayed behind in Makkah to return the trusts.
Amir bin Fuhaira served as their helper and Abdullah bin Uraiqit as their guide on the journey.
Who was the commander of the Muslim army in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk?
The Ghazwa of Tabuk (9 AH) was a campaign in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army of about 30,000. A Ghazwa is by definition a battle in which the Prophet personally took part.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was left in charge of Madina during the Tabuk expedition.
Who was the commander of the Quraysh army in the Battle of Uhud?
Abu Sufyan bin Harb led the Makkan army of about 3,000 in 3 AH, because Abu Jahl had been killed at Badr. Khalid bin Walid commanded the cavalry wing.
Abu Sufyan later accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.
Who was the first Ameer-ul-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful) in Islamic history?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was called Khalifa-tu-Rasul Allah, while Hazrat Umar (RA) was the first to be addressed as Ameer-ul-Momineen. Most Islamic history books record this.
The title was adopted by later caliphs such as Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
Who was the first caliph of Islam?
After the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, the Muslims chose Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) as their first caliph at Saqifa Bani Saida.
The four Rashidun caliphs ruled in the order Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali (RA).
Who was the first muezzin (caller to prayer) of Islam?
Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA), an Abyssinian companion, gave the first adhan in Madina after the Prophet approved it. Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the adhan in a dream.
Hazrat Bilal (RA) also gave the adhan from the roof of the Kaaba on the day Makkah was conquered.
Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg, for the electroweak theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim Nobel laureate in science.
Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 and is the youngest Nobel laureate.
Who was the first President of Pakistan?
Under the 1956 Constitution, Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956. Before this, the head of state was the Governor General.
Quaid-e-Azam and Ghulam Muhammad had served as Governor General, not as President.
Who was the first Pakistani woman to climb K2?
Samina Baig reached the summit of K2 on 22 July 2022, a few hours before Naila Kiani. She was the first Pakistani woman to do so.
Samina Baig had earlier climbed Mount Everest in 2013 and completed the Seven Summits in 2014.
Who was the first woman to travel to space?
Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. She orbited the Earth 48 times.
Sally Ride became the first American woman in space in 1983.
Who was the first woman officer of the Pakistan Army to be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General (three-star)?

Lt Gen Nigar Johar of the Army Medical Corps was promoted in June 2020 and became the first woman in the Pakistan Army to reach three-star rank. She was also appointed the first female Surgeon General of the Pakistan Army.
She is from Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Who was the guarantor and third party that brokered the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan?
The World Bank mediated the long negotiations and signed the treaty as a party for certain provisions. The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.
Some sources describe the World Bank's role as a broker rather than a strict guarantor.
Who was the head of state of Pakistan in 1960?
Ayub Khan took power in the October 1958 coup and was President of Pakistan in 1960. He remained in office until March 1969.
Iskander Mirza, the first President, was removed by Ayub Khan in October 1958.
Who headed the committee that compiled the Holy Quran in one book during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?

Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), on the advice of Hazrat Umar (RA) after the Battle of Yamama, assigned Hazrat Zaid bin Sabit (RA), the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran. He had memorised the Quran and written much of it down in the Prophet's lifetime.
Hazrat Usman (RA) later had standard copies prepared from this compilation.
Who was the false prophet and enemy leader fought by the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?

The Battle of Yamama in 12 AH was fought against the false claimant to prophethood Musaylima Kazzab and his tribe Banu Hanifa. The Muslim commander was Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA), and Musaylima was killed.
Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.
Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906 that presented Muslim demands to the Viceroy Lord Minto?

There are 30 people in a room and 2/3 of them are men. How many are women?
The women are 1/3 of the total, and 1/3 of 30 is 10.
Today is Monday the 1st of the month. What day will it be on the 12th of the month?
The 12th is 11 days after the 1st. 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, and 4 days after Monday is Friday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.
Today is Sunday. What will be the day after tomorrow?
Tomorrow is Monday, so the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
In Pakistan the working week traditionally runs Monday to Friday.
Total students are 1500 and 1200 of them are female. What is the percentage of females?
There are 24 students and 1/4 of them are male. What is the percentage of females?
Males are 1/4 = 25%, so females are 100 - 25 = 75% (18 of 24).
Total students in a class are 1500 and 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.
What are the two square roots of 64?
8 x 8 = 64 and (-8) x (-8) = 64, so the roots are +8 and -8.
Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.
To find 10% of a number, divide it by 10.
One tenth is the same as 10 percent.
BODMAS: brackets, orders, division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction.
One third of 120 is ten times larger than one third of one tenth of 120, which is 4.
What is the value of 2 + 2 x 2?
BODMAS gives multiplication priority over addition.
Division is done before addition under BODMAS.
What is the value of 2 x 3 + 3 x 6?
Both multiplications are done before the addition.
30% of 20 is 3 times 10% of 20, which is 2.
What is the value of 3 + 3 x 3?
Without BODMAS, one would wrongly compute (3 + 3) x 3 = 18.
60% is the same as 3/5, and 3/5 of 80 is 48.
90% of a number is the number minus 10% of it, so 9 - 0.9 = 8.1.
What is a chord that passes through the centre of a circle called?
A chord through the centre is the longest chord of the circle and is called the diameter.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is a quarter of one tenth of 90?
One tenth of 90 is 9, and a quarter of 9 is 9 / 4 = 2.25.
A quarter of one tenth is 1/40 of the number.
What is an angle greater than 90 degrees (and less than 180 degrees) called?
An angle between 90 and 180 degrees is obtuse.
An angle of exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle.
What is an angle less than 90 degrees called?
An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called an acute angle.
Two acute angles can add up to 90 degrees, in which case they are complementary.
What is a matrix whose entries are all zero called?
A matrix with every element equal to zero is called a null (zero) matrix.
Adding a null matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.
What is the value of cos 90 degrees?
On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), and its x-coordinate, the cosine, is 0.
What is cos x multiplied by tan x equal to?
Since tan x = sin x / cos x, cos x times tan x = sin x.
Another identity: sin x divided by cos x equals tan x.
What is the value of log 64 divided by log 4?
Write 64 as 4 cubed, so log 64 = 3 log 4. Therefore log 64 / log 4 = 3.
The change of base rule says log_b(a) = log a / log b, so this expression equals log base 4 of 64.
Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left.
A number divisible by 3 has digits whose sum is divisible by 3; 1+2+0 = 3.
What is the value of tan 0 degrees?
tan 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 = 0.
What is the 2nd letter of the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs A, B, C, so the second letter is B.
Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which is the 3rd letter?
The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The third letter is E.
MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.
What is the conjugate of a real number?
The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi. For a real number b = 0, so the conjugate is the same number.
A complex number equals its own conjugate only when it is real.
What is the common difference in the series 4, 7, 10, 13?
Such a series is called an arithmetic progression.
What is the distance between the points (-2, 0) and (-2, -3)?
The x-coordinates are equal, so the distance is |0 - (-3)| = 3. By formula: sqrt(0 + 9) = 3.
Points with the same x-coordinate lie on a vertical line.
Which is the distance formula between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
The distance comes from the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences.
The formula (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) gives the slope, and the midpoint uses averages.
What is the HCF of 18 and 24?
18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. The common factors are 2 and 3, so HCF = 6.
Their LCM is 72, and HCF x LCM = 18 x 24 = 432.
Division comes first: 2/3. Then 2 + 2/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 = 8/3, which is 2 and 2/3.
In BODMAS, division is performed before addition.
Which word is a synonym of extension?
Extension means an act of making something longer or larger, which is expansion.
The antonym of extension is reduction or curtailment.
Which word is a synonym of severely?
Severely means in a very strict or intense manner, which is harshly.
The antonym of severely is mildly or leniently.
Where does the line y = 3 + 5y lie?
Parallel to the x-axis, so it is neither axis
Rearranging gives -4y = 3, so y = -3/4. This is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, not the axis itself.
The x-axis is the line y = 0 and the y-axis is the line x = 0.
What comes next in the series: 1 X 2 Y Y 3 Z Z ?
The numbers 1, 2, 3 are followed by X once, Y twice and Z three times. So one more Z completes 3 ZZZ.
The letters follow the alphabetical order X, Y, Z.
Which comes next in the series: A2, D5, F9, ?
Letters move +3, +2, +1 (A, D, F, G) and numbers add 3, 4, 5 (2, 5, 9, 14). So the next term is G14.
In such series, check the letters and numbers separately.
Which is the odd one out: football, cricket, baseball, tennis?
Cricket, baseball and tennis are played by hitting the ball with a bat or racket. Football is played with the foot.
Football is the most widely played sport in the world.
Which is the odd one out: iron, brass, tin, copper?
Iron, tin and copper are pure metallic elements. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
Which letter comes immediately before W in the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs ... U, V, W, X, so V comes just before W.
W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.
Which letter comes next: A B C D E F G H ?
The letters are in alphabetical order, and the one after H is I.
I is the 9th letter of the alphabet.
In the series A1, C3, D4, G?, what number follows G?
Each number is the alphabet position of its letter: A=1, C=3, D=4, so G=7.
G is the 7th letter of the alphabet.
Which comes next in the series: A5, B10, C15, ?
Letters move forward one step (A, B, C, D) and numbers increase by 5 (5, 10, 15, 20). So the next is D20.
The number part is the table of 5.
Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)?
Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.
Letters like B, C, D, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line.
The numbers at odd places (105, 160, 225) rise by 55, then 65, so the next rise is 75: 225 + 75 = 300. The other numbers (55, 65, 75) rise by 10 each time.
Such interleaved series are solved by separating the odd and even places.
Two series are mixed: 115, 170 rise by 55, then 65 more, so 170 + 65 = 235. The other series 55, 65 would continue with 75 afterwards.
Here the added amount is the same as the number that follows each term: 115+55=170, 170+65=235.
Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.
The odd places 115, 225, 335 rise by 110 each time. The even places 55, 65 rise by 10, so the next is 75.
The question asks for the next term, which falls in the even-place series.
The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Hence 14 + 8 = 22.
When differences themselves form an arithmetic series, the series is quadratic.
The differences are 3, 6, 12, doubling each time, so the next difference is 24. Hence 45 - 24 = 21.
Series with doubling differences are common in verbal reasoning tests.
Which one is a prime number: 12, 25, 30, 37?
12 and 30 are even, and 25 = 5 x 5. 37 has no divisor other than 1 and itself, so it is prime.
2 is the only even prime number.
Which one is different: A12, B13, D15, E19, C14?
Letter position plus 11 gives the number: A(1)=12, B(2)=13, C(3)=14, D(4)=15. For E(5) it should be 16, but it is 19.
The odd one out breaks the pattern shared by all the others.
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, so the units cancel and it is dimensionless. The others all have units.
Velocity is measured in m/s, density in kg/m3 and pressure in pascals.
